Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the DORA client/authority disclosure content set; co-owned with the Insurance Product Manager for policyholder-facing wording, escalated to Regulatory Counsel for EU legal text

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Arts. 11(10), 14, 19(3) and 6(5) read on EUR-Lex consolidated text, plus Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 reporting templates and EIOPA's DORA guidance page, re-read at each content change (EU application date 17 January 2025)

In-scope processes.value: Product and correspondence change intake → DORA disclosure design gate: major-ICT-incident client notification templates, service-unavailability messages on the self-service portal, ICT third-party disclosure clauses in policyholder terms, and the Art. 11(10) aggregated cost-and-loss statement layout for the competent authority

In-scope systems.value: Master template library for EU-facing correspondence; rendered by the Policy Administration Platform and the Customer Self-Service Portal, with the approved inventory row held in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: DORA Disclosure Content Standard — one row per notice type (Art. 19(3) client incident notice, Art. 14 public/media statement, Art. 11(10) cost-and-loss estimate, Art. 28(3) third-party arrangement disclosure), each with mandatory content elements, language set, and the EU entity it is issued by

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Info Security Officer jointly; re-approved on every ESA/EIOPA template change and at minimum with the annual Art. 6(5) framework review

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Content must be live before the change it supports goes live; templates supporting Art. 19 reporting must satisfy the 4-hour/24-hour initial, 72-hour intermediate and one-month final windows, so no template may require data the firm cannot hold within 4 hours

Deadline reminders configured.value: GRC platform review task per template at T-30 days to any EU entity release, plus an automatic task whenever EIOPA or the national competent authority publishes a revised reporting template

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A notice issued from an unapproved or superseded template, or a template missing a mandatory Art. 19(3) element, is raised as a DORA control exception with root cause, owning team and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Counsel signs off every EU-facing template version and every remediation of a defective disclosure before it is re-published

checklist.step: Open the disclosure change record and pull the DORA trigger from the change request
actions: In the GRC platform open Regulatory Change ▸ DORA and create a disclosure change record for the request raised by the Insurance Product Manager or the Incident Response Lead.

Record on the header: EU legal entity and its national competent authority, affected lines of business, the trigger (new product, new ICT third-party arrangement, revised ESA template, post-incident lesson learned), and the target live date.
Ask the Incident Response Lead which incident-handling scenarios the change touches — client-impacting outage, data loss, payment interruption — and paste the answer into the Scope field.
Attach the signed change request and link the record to the DORA obligation node so the inventory row inherits the citation set.
checklist.done: the change record names the EU entity, the competent authority, the trigger and the incident scenarios, with the change request attached.

checklist.step: List every DORA-facing notice the change touches on the form inventory
actions: In OpenText open the EU Correspondence library and filter Metadata ▸ Regulation = DORA to list current template versions.

Add one inventory row per notice type touched: Art. 19(3) major-incident client notification, Art. 14 public/media statement, service-status banner on the Customer Self-Service Portal, ICT third-party disclosure clause in the policy terms, and the Art. 11(10) cost-and-loss estimate schedule.
On each row record template id, current version, owning team, delivery channel (email, portal, printed pack, broker bulletin) and language variants required for the entity's markets.
Mark rows NEW, AMEND or RETIRE and reject any row where the delivery channel has no owner named.
checklist.done: every touched notice has an inventory row with template id, version, channel, owner and language set.

checklist.step: Extract the mandatory content elements from the DORA articles and the ESA templates
actions: Open the EUR-Lex consolidated text of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 and read Art. 19(3), Art. 14(1)-(2) and Art. 11(10) in full.

For the client notice, list the elements the article demands: the fact of the major ICT-related incident, its actual or possible impact on the client's financial interests, the mitigation measures taken, and the contact route for questions.
Open Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 and lift the data fields the initial, intermediate and final reports require so the client notice never contradicts what the authority is told.
Write each element into the inventory row as a numbered requirement with its article reference and the date the text was read.
Flag any element that depends on a delegated act still in draft and note the source you will re-check.
checklist.done: each inventory row carries a numbered, article-cited list of mandatory content elements with a read date.

checklist.step: Draft the client-facing wording for the Art. 19(3) major-incident notice
actions: Draft the notice against the numbered element list, keeping placeholders for incident reference, detection time, services affected, client impact and expected restoration.

Write plain-language sentences describing the impact on the client's financial interests — payment delay, claim settlement delay, inability to transact — rather than describing internal ICT failure modes.
State the mitigation measures already taken and the next update time so the notice can be issued without undue delay while facts are still incomplete.
Send the draft to the Incident Response Lead to confirm the placeholders map to data available in the incident record within 4 hours of classification.
Produce the language variants for every market the EU entity writes in and log the translation vendor and date.
checklist.done: a placeholder-complete draft exists in every required language, with placeholders confirmed as fillable within the 4-hour window.

checklist.step: Draft the Art. 14 public and counterparty communication variants
actions: Draft the public/media holding statement and the counterparty notice from the same element list, stripping any detail that would expose an unremediated vulnerability.
Name in the template the person designated under Art. 14(2) as responsible for implementing the communication strategy and acting as public and media contact, with their deputy.
Add the broker and distribution-partner variant to be issued through the Broker & Agent Portal so intermediaries answer clients consistently.
Route the drafts to the Chief Info Security Officer to confirm no disclosed detail aids an attacker.
checklist.done: public, counterparty and broker variants exist, each naming the Art. 14(2) designated contact and cleared by the CISO.

checklist.step: Build the Art. 11(10) aggregated cost-and-loss statement layout
actions: Design the statement as a fixed schedule: gross costs and losses from major ICT-related incidents for the financial year, recoveries received, and net figures, split by incident reference.

Define each cost line against the recognised categories — direct remediation and forensics, replaced hardware and software, redress and compensation paid to clients, contractual penalties, legal and advisory fees, and lost revenue from service unavailability.
Agree the extraction rule with the Controller: each line ties to a general-ledger account and cost centre in the ERP so the figure is reproducible from the books.
Add a methodology note stating the estimation basis for any modelled figure and the incident classification source used to decide what counts as major.
checklist.done: the statement layout names every cost line, its ledger source and the estimation basis, and reconciles by design to the GL.

checklist.step: Write the ICT third-party disclosure clauses into policyholder and counterparty terms
actions: Open the EU clause library in Icertis and locate the ICT services and data-location clause set used for policyholder terms and outsourcing counterparties.
Update the clause so it discloses the use of ICT third-party service providers supporting critical or important functions and the client's route to information about service continuity.
Cross-check the clause against the Art. 30 contractual requirements already imposed on the provider so the two documents cannot contradict each other.
Publish the clause as a locked library item and record the version number on the form inventory row.
checklist.done: the disclosure clause is published as a locked Icertis library version and referenced from the inventory row.

checklist.step: Map every mandatory element to a data field that the source systems can actually supply
actions: For each placeholder, name the source: incident record fields in ServiceNow (incident number, detection timestamp, classification decision, affected services from the CMDB), client records in the Policy Administration Platform, and outage windows from the service-status feed.
Confirm with the IT Service Delivery Manager that each named field is populated at classification time, not at closure.
Where a placeholder has no reliable source, either change the wording or raise a data-capture requirement against the incident form — never leave a template that can only be filled by hand.
Record the field-to-placeholder map as an attachment on the change record.
checklist.done: every placeholder has a named populated source field, or a raised data-capture requirement with an owner.

checklist.step: Define the client-population selection rule that decides who gets the notice
actions: Write the rule that turns an affected service into an affected client list: policies serviced by the affected application, claims in flight, payments queued in the outage window, and portal sessions failed.
Agree with the Data Protection Officer the lawful basis and the contact channel precedence (registered email, portal message, postal) and the treatment of clients with no digital contact record.
Specify the broker-intermediated case: notice to the client with a parallel bulletin to the broker of record.
Document the rule with a worked example on a past incident and get the Incident Response Lead to confirm it is executable during a live incident.
checklist.done: a documented, worked selection rule exists that produces a named client list from an affected service.

checklist.step: Run legal, privacy and CISO review on the full template set
actions: Circulate every draft version with its numbered element list to Regulatory Counsel, the Data Protection Officer and the Chief Info Security Officer with a fixed 5-business-day review window.
Log each reviewer comment on the change record with an accept/reject decision and the reason.
Re-check each accepted edit against the element list so a wording improvement cannot delete a mandatory element.
Hold the release where any reviewer objection is unresolved rather than shipping with an open comment.
checklist.done: every draft carries dated legal, privacy and CISO reviews with all comments dispositioned.

checklist.step: Obtain the approval that authorises publication
actions: Review the element-to-wording conformance grid and the reviewer dispositions for each template version.
Approve or reject each version individually and record name, role and date on the GRC change record.
Where the change alters what the management body has approved under Art. 6(5), route a summary to the Corporate Secretary for the next board ICT risk item.
Release only approved versions to the document management library.
checklist.done: each published version carries a named, dated Head of Compliance approval on the change record.

checklist.step: Publish the approved versions and retire the superseded ones
actions: Check the approved version into the EU Correspondence library with metadata: regulation = DORA, article, entity, language, effective date, approver.
Set the superseded version to Retired with a retirement date and remove it from the render path used by the Policy Administration Platform and the Customer Self-Service Portal.
Ask the Configuration Engineer to confirm the render path now points at the new version id in each environment.
Confirm no retired version remains reachable by any correspondence job.
checklist.done: only approved versions are reachable from the render path and every superseded version is dated and retired.

checklist.step: Proof the templates end to end with real placeholder data
actions: Raise a rehearsal incident in the test environment, classify it as major, and let the notice generate through the normal path.
Inspect the rendered output in each channel and each language for blank placeholders, truncated text, broken merge fields and misplaced entity or authority names.
Time the render from classification to first output and confirm it fits inside the 4-hour initial-notification window.
Log defects on the change record and re-test after fix; do not sign the release on a partial pass.
checklist.done: every channel and language renders complete output from rehearsal data inside the 4-hour window.

checklist.step: Refresh the form inventory as the single register of DORA disclosures
actions: Update the DORA form inventory with the published version id, effective date, article references, channels, languages, entity and approver for every row.
Close retired rows with a retirement date and the id of the version that replaced them.
Reconcile the inventory row count to the OpenText library query for regulation = DORA and resolve any difference before closing the change.
Publish the refreshed inventory to the Compliance and Operational Resilience distribution list.
checklist.done: the inventory reconciles to the document library with no unexplained rows and the change record is closed.

checklist.step: File the evidence pack under the DORA retention rule
actions: Move the change record export, approved versions, element lists with citation captures, reviewer dispositions and rehearsal render outputs into the repository under DORA / Disclosures / <entity> / <year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-retirement retention label so the pack survives template replacement and entity reorganisation.
Confirm the index makes the pack searchable by template id, article and entity.
Notify the Head of Compliance that the pack is filed and immutable.
checklist.done: the evidence pack is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by template id, article and entity.

testing.step: Build the population of DORA-facing template versions released in the period
actions: Extract from the OpenText version history every template version with regulation = DORA and a check-in date inside the period, across all EU entities and languages.
Add the render-path configuration history from the Policy Administration Platform and the Customer Self-Service Portal so a version pushed without a library check-in cannot hide.
Reconcile the extract to the GRC form inventory and to the release notes for the period, and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the inventory and the release notes and signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile every live template to an approved inventory row
actions: Match each population row to a GRC inventory row on template id plus version and confirm the approval date pre-dates the effective date.
List any live version with no inventory row, no approval, or an approval dated after go-live as an automatic exception.
Confirm each retired version is genuinely unreachable by querying the render path for retired version ids.
testing.done: every live version matches an approved, pre-dated inventory row or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of Art. 19(3) client-notice and Art. 14 public-statement versions — these are the ones that carry client impact.
Take 15 further versions at random from the remaining population using a recorded seed, minimum 25 versions in total, with at least one non-English language variant per entity.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all client-facing versions and includes non-English variants.

testing.step: Re-perform the element extraction from the primary legal text
actions: Open the EUR-Lex consolidated text of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 and independently derive the mandatory elements of Art. 19(3), Art. 14 and Art. 11(10) without reading the firm's element list first.
Compare your derived list to the list recorded on the sampled inventory row; a missing element, a wrong article reference or a stale citation is an exception.
Check whether Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 or a later ESA template revision changed any field since the recorded read date.
Capture the EUR-Lex page and its consolidation date into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independently derived element list and a captured, dated source text.

testing.step: Grade each sampled template element by element against the wording
actions: Build a grid of sampled version against mandatory element and mark each cell present, partial or absent, quoting the sentence that satisfies it.
Fail any template that describes the incident without stating the actual or possible impact on the client's financial interests or the mitigation measures taken.
Check the language variants say the same thing — compare the translated notice back to the approved source using the translation vendor's certification.
Record every partial or absent cell as an exception with the template id and element number.
testing.done: a complete element-by-element grid exists with a quoted sentence behind every 'present' mark.

testing.step: Trace each placeholder to a populated source field in a live incident record
actions: Pick two closed major ICT-related incidents from the period and open their ServiceNow records.
For each placeholder in the sampled templates, read the mapped field on the incident record and confirm it was populated at the classification timestamp, not only at closure.
Where a placeholder maps to a field first populated after classification, record it as a fail — the template cannot be filled inside the 4-hour window.
Screenshot the incident record field values with their audit history into the workpaper.
testing.done: every placeholder is proven fillable from fields populated at classification, or the gap is logged as a fail.

testing.step: Recompute the Art. 11(10) statement from the general ledger
actions: Extract the ledger accounts and cost centres named in the statement layout for the financial year and total them by incident reference.
Compare your total to the figure the statement layout would produce and explain any difference over 1% of gross costs.
Confirm recoveries are shown separately and are not netted into gross costs, and that the estimation basis note covers every modelled figure.
Confirm the incident references used are exactly those classified major under the Art. 18 criteria in the period.
testing.done: the statement reconciles to the ledger within 1% with recoveries shown gross and every modelled figure explained.

testing.step: Re-perform the render and time it against the notification window
actions: Generate each sampled template in the test environment from a rehearsal major incident and inspect the output in every channel.
Record the elapsed time from classification to first rendered client output and compare it to the 4-hour initial-notification window and the without-undue-delay standard in Art. 19(3).
Confirm the client-population selection rule returns a client list, not an error, when the affected service has in-flight claims and queued payments.
Log blank placeholders, truncation and wrong-entity headers as exceptions with screenshots.
testing.done: every sampled template renders complete inside the window, with the timing recorded in the workpaper.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one GRC issue per exception carrying the template id, version, element number, the failure and the client-impact consequence.

Assign a root cause — element list not refreshed after an ESA template change, unapproved version pushed to the render path, placeholder with no populated source, translation drift — and an owning team.
Set a remediation date inside 30 days for any client-facing defect and notify the Head of Compliance the same day.
Carry every open issue into the next release-wave test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance thresholds for missing mandatory elements and unapproved live versions.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the grid, the render timings and the ledger reconciliation.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored and approved none of the sampled versions, sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open client-facing defect to the ICT Risk Committee and file the workpaper under DORA / Art. 19(3) disclosures.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, exception rate and committee reporting date exists in the repository.

In-scope processes.value: Major-incident notification run: classification decision → affected-client population build → notice generation and dispatch → authority initial/intermediate/final reports → notice log closure, for every incident classified major in any EU insurance or reinsurance entity

In-scope systems.value: Client population and contact data plus correspondence dispatch; incident timestamps come from ServiceNow ITSM and the notice log row is held in the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Major ICT Incident Client Notification Runbook — trigger, 4-hour and 24-hour clocks, population build query, channel precedence, bounce handling, broker parallel bulletin, and the notice log fields that must be completed before stand-down

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Info Security Officer and the Head of Compliance; re-approved after every major incident post-mortem and at the annual Art. 6(5) framework review

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Initial notification to the competent authority within 4 hours of classification as major and no later than 24 hours from becoming aware; intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial; final report no later than one month after the intermediate; client notice under Art. 19(3) without undue delay, targeted inside 4 hours of classification

Deadline reminders configured.value: ServiceNow SLA timers armed at the classification click — 4h, 24h, 72h and one-month clocks with escalation to the Incident Response Lead at 50% and to the CISO at 75% of each window

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is event-driven; testing runs monthly over that month's classified incidents with a full-period re-sweep before the annual framework review

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly notification-timeliness workpaper (incident extract, clock recomputation, population completeness test, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under DORA / Art. 19 notifications

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Notice log export with incident reference, classification timestamp, dispatch timestamps by channel, client counts and authority submission receipts, presentable to the national competent authority within 2 business days of request

checklist.step: Take the classification decision and start the reporting clocks
actions: In ServiceNow open the incident and complete the DORA Classification form against the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 criteria: clients and counterparties affected, data losses, duration and service downtime, geographical spread, economic impact, criticality of services affected, reputational impact.
Record the awareness timestamp (when the firm first became aware) and the classification timestamp separately — the 24-hour clock runs from awareness, the 4-hour clock from classification.
Set Major = Yes/No with the criteria met listed, and have a second responder countersign the decision in the record.
Confirm the SLA timers for 4h, 24h, 72h and one month have armed on the record and that escalation contacts resolve to on-call people, not vacant queues.
checklist.done: the incident carries awareness and classification timestamps, a countersigned major/not-major decision with criteria, and four armed clocks.

checklist.step: Stand up the notification cell and assign the named roles
actions: Open the DORA notification bridge and add: Incident Response Lead, Policy Admin Ops Lead, Communications Specialist, Regulatory Counsel, Data Protection Officer and the Art. 14(2) designated public contact.
Assign on the incident record who drafts the client notice, who builds the population, who dispatches, and who submits the authority report.
Post the four deadline timestamps into the bridge in UTC and local entity time so nobody miscounts across time zones.
Start a running decision log in the bridge channel that will be exported into the evidence pack.
checklist.done: the bridge is live with named owners for draft, population, dispatch and authority filing, and the deadlines posted in UTC.

checklist.step: Build the affected-client population from the affected services
actions: Read the affected configuration items from the CMDB entry on the incident and translate them into the business services and products they support.

Run the notification population query for the outage window: policies serviced by the affected application, claims with activity in the window, premium and benefit payments queued or failed, and failed portal or contact-centre transactions.
Deduplicate to one row per client with policy references, preferred language, contact channel precedence and broker of record.
Save the extract with its query text, run timestamp and row count as the population of record and hand the count to the notification bridge.
checklist.done: a deduplicated client population exists with its query, run timestamp and row count recorded on the incident.

checklist.step: Fill the approved notice template and clear it for issue
actions: Open the current approved Art. 19(3) template version from the EU Correspondence library — never a local copy.

Fill the placeholders from the incident record: incident reference, services affected, impact on the client's financial interests, mitigation measures taken so far, next update time and the contact route.
Send the filled draft to Regulatory Counsel and the CISO on a 30-minute clearance clock; record both clearances on the incident.
Where facts are still moving, issue on what is known with a stated next update rather than holding the notice — Art. 19(3) requires notification without undue delay.
checklist.done: a filled notice cleared by counsel and the CISO exists inside the 4-hour target, with the template version id recorded.

checklist.step: Dispatch the client notices across every channel in precedence order
actions: Load the population extract into the correspondence job and select the cleared template version and language variants.
Dispatch in channel precedence: registered email, then secure portal message on the Customer Self-Service Portal, then postal for clients with no digital contact record.
Record per client the dispatch timestamp, channel and message id returned by the gateway.
Do not suppress any client on the extract without a written instruction from the Data Protection Officer recorded on the incident.
checklist.done: every client on the extract has a dispatch timestamp, channel and message id, with no undocumented suppressions.

checklist.step: Issue the broker, counterparty and public variants
actions: Publish the broker bulletin to the Broker & Agent Portal for every broker of record on the population, so intermediaries answer client calls consistently.
Send the counterparty variant to reinsurers, outsourcing partners and payment counterparties identified by the Incident Response Lead.
Release the Art. 14 public statement only through the designated public and media contact, and log the release time.
Brief the contact centre with the same facts and an approved holding script before the first client notice lands.
checklist.done: broker, counterparty, public and contact-centre channels all carry the same cleared facts, each with a release timestamp.

checklist.step: Submit the initial notification to the competent authority
actions: Complete the initial notification on the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 template: incident reference, entity identifiers including LEI, classification criteria met, incident start and detection times, services and clients affected, and whether the incident is ongoing.
Submit through the national competent authority's DORA reporting channel within 4 hours of classification and in any case within 24 hours of awareness.
Save the submission receipt or reference number returned by the authority onto the incident record and the notice log.
Where the channel is unavailable, use the authority's documented fallback route and record the attempt times — never let the window lapse silently.
checklist.done: the initial notification is submitted inside the window with an authority receipt reference filed on the incident.

checklist.step: Submit the intermediate report within 72 hours
actions: Gather from the incident record the updated status, the root-cause hypothesis, the classification criteria as now measured, and the recovery actions taken.
Quantify to the extent known: clients affected, transactions affected, downtime duration, data losses and economic impact, using the same measurement basis as the classification.
Submit the intermediate report within 72 hours of the initial notification, or earlier if regular activities have been recovered.
File the receipt and note on the incident whether any figure changed materially from the initial notification and why.
checklist.done: the intermediate report is submitted within 72 hours with quantified impact and its receipt filed.

checklist.step: Submit the final report within one month
actions: Take the completed root-cause analysis from the post-incident review and the final measured impact figures from Finance and Operations.
Complete the final report: root causes, remediation applied and planned, permanent fixes, final cost and loss figures, and the lessons-learned actions with owners.
Submit no later than one month after the intermediate report and file the receipt.
Feed the final cost and loss figures into the Art. 11(10) aggregated annual cost-and-loss statement so the two never diverge.
checklist.done: the final report is submitted within one month, its receipt filed, and its cost figures posted to the annual aggregate.

checklist.step: Work the undelivered notices until every affected client is reached
actions: Pull the bounce and delivery-failure report from the correspondence gateway within 24 hours of dispatch.
Re-issue on the next channel in precedence and, where no channel remains, raise an outbound call task in Genesys with the approved script.
Record the final outcome per client — delivered, re-issued and delivered, or unreachable with reason and attempts.
Escalate any client still unreached after 5 business days to the Policy Admin Ops Lead for a documented decision.
checklist.done: every client is delivered, re-issued or documented as unreachable with attempts, with none left in bounce state.

checklist.step: Close the notice log row with the complete timing record
actions: Complete the notice log row: incident reference, awareness and classification timestamps, template version id, population row count, first and last dispatch timestamps by channel, client counts delivered and unreachable, and the three authority submission receipts.
Compute and record elapsed hours from classification to first client dispatch and from awareness to initial authority notification.
Attach the population extract, dispatch report, bounce report and receipts to the row.
Set the row to Closed only when no field is blank and no client remains in bounce state.
checklist.done: the notice log row is complete with computed elapsed times and every artefact attached.

checklist.step: Flag and self-assess any breach of a notification window
actions: Compare each recorded elapsed time against its window — 4h, 24h, 72h, one month, and without undue delay for the client notice.
Raise a DORA breach record for each window missed, with the number of clients affected and the reason for the delay.
Ask Regulatory Counsel whether a self-report to the competent authority is required and record the answer with its date.
Never close a missed window as a documentation issue — the record must state that the obligation was missed.
checklist.done: every missed window has a breach record, a client-impact count and a counsel-recorded self-report decision.

checklist.step: Run the post-incident review on the notification path itself
actions: Hold the review within 10 business days of the final report, with the notification cell and the contact centre present.
Walk the timeline minute by minute and identify where time was lost: classification hesitation, population query runtime, clearance loops, gateway throughput.
Raise actions with owners and dates against each loss, and update the runbook where the sequence itself was wrong.
Feed the actions into the Art. 13 learning-and-evolving record and into the next training cycle.
checklist.done: a dated review exists with a minute-level timeline, owned actions and a runbook revision decision.

checklist.step: Rehearse the notification path between real incidents
actions: Run a quarterly no-notice rehearsal: inject a simulated client-impacting outage and require the full path from classification through dispatch and a dry-run authority submission.
Measure the same clocks as a live incident and record the elapsed times against the 4h/24h windows.
Test the fallback route for the authority channel and the postal path for clients with no digital contact record.
Publish the rehearsal result to the ICT Risk Committee with any capability gap named.
checklist.done: a quarterly rehearsal record exists with measured clock times and named gaps reported to the committee.

checklist.step: File the incident notification evidence pack
actions: Move the notice log row export, population extract with query, dispatch and bounce reports, cleared notice renders, bridge decision log and the three authority receipts into DORA / Notifications / <entity> / <incident reference>.
Apply the 10-years-from-incident-closure retention label.
Confirm the pack is searchable by incident reference, entity and classification date.
Confirm immutability so timestamps cannot be edited after filing.
checklist.done: the pack is filed immutably under the incident reference with a 10-year label and is searchable.

testing.step: Build the population of classified ICT incidents for the period
actions: Extract every incident in the period with a DORA Classification form completed, including not-major decisions, with awareness and classification timestamps and the criteria recorded.
Add all P1/P2 incidents and all service-availability breaches from the monitoring feed that have no classification form, so unclassified incidents surface.
Reconcile the extract to the major-incident count in the notice log and to the SOC's incident register, and resolve every difference before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles across ServiceNow, the notice log and the SOC register and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Challenge the not-major classifications before testing timeliness
actions: Take every incident classified not-major with client impact, data loss or downtime over one hour.
Re-apply the Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 criteria and thresholds independently using the measured impact figures.
Any incident that meets the major thresholds but was classified not-major is a fail — an unreported major incident, not a classification difference of opinion.
Record the recomputed criteria values against the recorded ones for each challenged incident.
testing.done: every not-major call with material impact is independently re-applied and any misclassification is raised as a fail.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of major incidents and notices
actions: Take 100% of incidents classified major in the period — the population is small and each one carries a reporting obligation.
Within each, draw 25 client notices at random using a recorded seed, stratified across channels and languages.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: all major incidents are in scope and the client-notice sample is reproducible and channel-stratified.

testing.step: Recompute every clock from the underlying timestamps
actions: Read awareness and classification timestamps from the incident audit history, not from the summary fields, and normalise everything to UTC.

Recompute: classification to initial authority notification against 4 hours, awareness to initial against 24 hours, initial to intermediate against 72 hours, intermediate to final against one month, and classification to first client dispatch.
Compare each recomputed elapsed time to the notice log figure and treat any difference as an exception in itself.
Check for backdated edits to timestamp fields in the audit history and flag any found.
testing.done: every clock is recomputed from audit-history timestamps and reconciles to the notice log, with no backdating found.

testing.step: Test the affected-client population for completeness
actions: Re-run the notification population query for the sampled incident's outage window and affected services, independently of the saved extract.
Compare your row count and client ids to the extract of record and investigate every difference.
Cross-check against a second source: failed payment records for the window and contact-centre contacts citing the outage, to find clients the query missed.
Any client with impact evidence who is absent from the notified population is a fail.
testing.done: the population is independently re-derived and every difference against the extract of record is explained or raised.

testing.step: Trace each sampled notice to a dispatch record and an approved template version
actions: For each sampled client, open the correspondence history and read the dispatch timestamp, channel and gateway message id.
Confirm the template version used matches the approved version in the OpenText library on the dispatch date.
Open the rendered document and confirm it names the incident, the impact on the client's financial interests, the mitigation measures and the contact route.
Confirm bounced notices were re-issued and closed out, and capture the correspondence history screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled notice traces to a dispatch record, an approved template version and a complete rendered document.

testing.step: Verify the three authority submissions against their receipts
actions: For each major incident, open the initial, intermediate and final submissions and read the authority reference numbers and submission timestamps from the receipts.
Confirm the entity identifiers and LEI on each submission match the entity that suffered the incident.
Compare the impact figures on the intermediate and final reports to the incident record and the ledger-based cost figures, and query any unexplained change.
Any missing receipt is treated as a non-submission until the authority reference is produced.
testing.done: all three submissions per major incident are evidenced by authority receipts with matching entity identifiers.

testing.step: Test the rehearsal programme and the fallback routes
actions: Confirm a rehearsal was run in each quarter of the period and read the measured clock times from each rehearsal record.
Check the fallback authority submission route and the postal client path were exercised at least once.
Compare rehearsal elapsed times to live-incident elapsed times and flag where live performance is materially worse than rehearsed.
Confirm every gap named in a rehearsal has an owned action with a date.
testing.done: quarterly rehearsals are evidenced with measured times, fallbacks exercised and every named gap owned.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception with the incident reference, the window missed or the clients unnotified, and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause — classification delay, population query gap, clearance loop, gateway failure, submission channel outage — and an owning team.
For any missed authority window or unnotified client, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel and record the outcome.
Carry every open issue into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and, where required, a self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute on-time rates for each of the four windows and the client-notification completeness rate, against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the recomputed clocks, the population re-derivation and the authority receipts.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled none of the sampled incidents, sign the workpaper.
Report to the ICT Risk Committee and the management body's risk agenda, and file under DORA / Art. 19 notifications.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with on-time rates, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Translate each DORA article into named configuration objects
actions: Take the article list from Regulatory Counsel — Arts. 17-19 plus Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 — and open a traceability matrix.

For each requirement name the object that will enforce it: a mandatory field on the DORA Classification form, an SLA definition, an escalation rule, a notification flow, or a field in the report export map.

Write the expected production value for each object — for example the SLA definition 'DORA initial notification' with a 4-hour duration measured from the classification field, and 'DORA awareness limit' with 24 hours measured from the awareness field.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the mapping covers every reporting field before any build starts.
checklist.done: every requirement has a named configuration object with an expected value and a counsel-confirmed mapping.

checklist.step: Build the DORA classification form with the criteria as mandatory inputs
actions: In the non-production instance open Incident ▸ Form Layout and add the DORA Classification section.

Add mandatory fields for each Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 criterion: clients and financial counterparties affected (count and share), data losses, duration and service downtime, geographical spread by Member State, economic impact, criticality of services affected, and reputational impact.
Add separate, non-editable-after-save timestamp fields for awareness and for classification, each stamped by the platform clock in UTC.
Add the Major = Yes/No field with a second-responder countersign field, and make the incident unresolvable while the section is incomplete.
checklist.done: the classification section captures every criterion, stamps both timestamps immutably, and blocks resolution when incomplete.

checklist.step: Encode the materiality thresholds so the system proposes the classification
actions: Create a business rule that evaluates the entered criterion values against the thresholds in the Delegated Regulation and proposes Major = Yes when the required combination is met.
Store each threshold as a controlled configuration value with the article reference in its description, not as a literal buried in script.
Allow a responder to override the proposal only with a mandatory free-text justification and an automatic notification to the Incident Response Lead.
Log every proposal, override and justification to an audit table that responders cannot edit.
checklist.done: the system proposes a classification from encoded thresholds and every override is justified and audit-logged.

checklist.step: Define the four statutory SLA timers against the correct start events
actions: Create SLA definitions: initial notification 4 hours from the classification timestamp; awareness limit 24 hours from the awareness timestamp; intermediate report 72 hours from the initial submission timestamp; final report one month from the intermediate submission timestamp.
Set all four to run on a 24x7 schedule with no business-hours calendar and no pause-on-hold condition — statutory clocks do not pause for weekends.
Restrict the ability to cancel or reset an SLA to a role held only by the CISO's delegate, and log every such action.
Configure escalation notifications at 50% and 75% of each window to the Incident Response Lead and then the CISO.
checklist.done: all four timers run 24x7 from the correct start events, cannot be paused, and escalate at 50% and 75%.

checklist.step: Wire the affected-service lookup to the CMDB so scope is derived, not typed
actions: Confirm every application supporting a critical or important function carries the criticality attribute and the owning business service in the CMDB.
Configure the incident form so selecting affected configuration items automatically populates the business services, the criticality flag and the client-facing indicator.
Feed that derived scope into the classification criteria for criticality of services affected, so a responder cannot understate scope by typing a narrower answer.
Ask the Third-Party Risk Manager to confirm ICT third-party provided services are represented in the CMDB with their provider named.
checklist.done: affected scope and criticality derive from CMDB relationships, including third-party provided services.

checklist.step: Build the notification workflow that fires the client and authority tasks
actions: Create a flow triggered on Major = Yes that opens tasks for population build, notice clearance, dispatch and the three authority submissions, each pre-assigned to the runbook role and pre-dated to its window.
Call the Policy Administration Platform correspondence API with the incident reference and affected services so the population query can start without manual hand-off.
Prevent the flow from completing the dispatch task until an approved template version id is recorded on the incident.
Handle API failure by raising a high-priority task to the Policy Admin Ops Lead rather than failing silently.
checklist.done: Major = Yes opens all pre-dated tasks, triggers the population build, and cannot close dispatch without an approved template id.

checklist.step: Map the export field set to the ESA reporting template
actions: Build the export map from incident fields to every field of the Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 initial, intermediate and final templates, including entity identifiers and LEI.
Add validation that blocks the export where a mandatory template field is empty, naming the field in the error rather than failing generically.
Version the map with the template version it satisfies so a template revision forces a new map version.
Run a sample export against a closed test incident and have the Regulatory Reporting Manager confirm every field lands in the right template box.
checklist.done: the export map is versioned to the ESA template, validates mandatory fields, and is confirmed field-by-field by reporting.

checklist.step: Lock down who may change a DORA configuration object
actions: Restrict write access on the classification form, threshold values, SLA definitions and export map to a dedicated DORA configuration role.
Remove standing access for general platform administrators and route any need through privileged access with a time-boxed check-out.
Attest the role membership quarterly with the Chief Info Security Officer as approver and remove leavers within 24 hours.
Alert the SOC on any change to the role membership or any direct table edit outside a change record.
checklist.done: write access is limited to an attested DORA role, standing admin access is removed and out-of-change edits alert the SOC.

checklist.step: Test the configuration in non-production against scripted scenarios
actions: Write scenarios covering: threshold just below and just above each criterion, an override of the proposed classification, an incident spanning a weekend, and an incident affecting a third-party provided service.
Execute each scenario and record the classification proposed, the timers armed, the tasks opened and the export validation result.
Assert the weekend scenario proves the 24x7 clock did not pause, and the override scenario proves the justification and audit entry were captured.
Attach the evidence to the change record; a scenario without recorded evidence counts as not executed.
checklist.done: every scenario is executed with recorded results, including a weekend clock and an override case.

checklist.step: Take the change through CAB with the regulatory mapping attached
actions: Raise a normal change with the traceability matrix, the test evidence and a rollback plan attached.
Add the Chief Info Security Officer and the Head of Compliance as mandatory approvers on any change touching a threshold, a timer or the export map.
Present at CAB the specific statutory window each object enforces and what breaks if the change is wrong.
Refuse promotion where any mandatory approval or test evidence is missing.
checklist.done: the change is CAB-approved with CISO and Compliance approvals and complete test evidence attached.

checklist.step: Promote to production and verify the live values immediately
actions: Promote the update set in the approved window and record the promotion timestamp and the update set id.
Immediately export the production values of every affected object and compare them line by line to the approved standard.
Raise a rehearsal incident in production, classify it major, and confirm the four timers arm and the tasks open, then cancel it with the cancellation logged.
Roll back on any mismatch rather than fixing forward in production.
checklist.done: production values match the approved standard and a production rehearsal proves the timers and tasks fire.

checklist.step: Update the DORA Configuration Standard as the single source of expected values
actions: Update the standard page with the new expected values, the article each implements, the change record id and the promotion date.
Retire superseded rows with a date and the id of the change that replaced them.
Publish the revision to the Operational Resilience, Compliance and Internal Audit distribution lists.
Link the standard from the GRC control record so testers use the same expected values.
checklist.done: the standard states current expected values with article references and change ids, and is linked from the GRC control.

checklist.step: Run automated drift detection against the standard
actions: Schedule a weekly export of the classification fields, thresholds, SLA definitions, escalation rules and export map from production.
Compare the export to the standard and raise an alert naming the object, the expected value and the found value on any difference.
Alert immediately on any SLA cancellation, threshold edit or direct table update that has no linked change record.
Route alerts to the SOC Lead with the IT Service Delivery Manager on the escalation path.
checklist.done: weekly drift comparison runs, names differences object by object, and out-of-change edits alert in real time.

checklist.step: Remediate drift under change control, never by silent edit
actions: Open a GRC exception for each drift finding with the object, the expected and found values, and the period the wrong value was live.
Assess whether any incident was classified or timed under the wrong value and, if so, notify the Incident Response Lead and Compliance the same day.
Restore the approved value through an emergency change with CISO approval and record the restoration timestamp.
Close the exception only after a re-export confirms the value is correct and the impact assessment is written.
checklist.done: every drift has an exception, an impact assessment on affected incidents, a CISO-approved restoration and a verified re-export.

checklist.step: File the configuration evidence pack
actions: Move the traceability matrix, test evidence, CAB approvals, promotion records, production exports and drift reports into DORA / Configuration / <year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-retirement retention label to each configuration version.
Confirm the pack is searchable by configuration object, article and change record id.
Confirm the exports are stored immutably so a later edit cannot rewrite history.
checklist.done: the pack is filed immutably, retention-labelled and searchable by object, article and change id.

testing.step: Build the population of DORA configuration changes and objects
actions: Extract every change record in the period whose update set touched the classification form, threshold values, SLA definitions, escalation rules or export map.
Extract the platform audit log for direct table edits to the same objects so changes made outside a change record surface.
Reconcile the two extracts and treat any audited edit without a change record as an automatic exception before sampling.
testing.done: the change population reconciles to the platform audit log with every out-of-change edit already listed.

testing.step: Compare the full production configuration to the approved standard
actions: Export the live values of every object named in the DORA Configuration Standard as at the test date.
Compare object by object to the approved expected values and list every difference with expected, found and last-modified-by.
Confirm each of the four SLA definitions uses the correct start field, the correct duration, a 24x7 schedule and no pause condition.
Attach the raw export to the workpaper so the comparison can be re-run.
testing.done: a line-by-line comparison of live values to the standard exists with the raw export attached.

testing.step: Draw and document the change sample
actions: Take 100% of changes touching a threshold value, an SLA definition or the export map.
Take 10 further changes at random from the remainder using a recorded seed, minimum 20 in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every threshold, timer and export-map change.

testing.step: Re-perform the requirement-to-object mapping from the legal text
actions: Read Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 and independently list the classification criteria and thresholds without consulting the traceability matrix.
Compare your list to the encoded threshold values in production and raise any missing criterion or wrong threshold as an exception.
Read Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 and confirm every mandatory report field has a source field in the export map.
Capture the source texts and their consolidation dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: criteria, thresholds and report fields are independently derived and reconciled to the live configuration.

testing.step: Re-perform the timers with scripted scenarios in a controlled instance
actions: In a cloned production instance raise incidents that classify major on a Friday evening and on a public holiday.
Record when each of the four timers breaches and confirm the elapsed wall-clock time matches 4h, 24h, 72h and one month with no pause.
Attempt to cancel an SLA as a general platform administrator and confirm the action is denied and alerted.
Screenshot each timer state and the denial event into the workpaper.
testing.done: the timers are proven to run 24x7 from the correct start fields and cannot be cancelled by a general administrator.

testing.step: Test the classification proposal and override controls
actions: Enter criterion values just below and just above each threshold and record the classification the system proposes.
Compare the proposals to the Delegated Regulation thresholds and raise any wrong proposal as a fail.
Override a proposal and confirm the justification is mandatory, the Incident Response Lead is notified, and the audit entry is written and non-editable.
Sample 10 real overrides from the period and read whether the justification actually addresses the criterion.
testing.done: proposals match the regulation at the boundaries and every override is justified, notified and audit-logged.

testing.step: Trace sampled changes to CAB approval, test evidence and post-implementation verification
actions: For each sampled change open the record and confirm CISO and Head of Compliance approvals exist and pre-date the promotion timestamp.
Confirm the scenario test evidence is attached and covers the object actually changed, not a related one.
Confirm a post-implementation production export exists and matches the standard as revised by that change.
Any change promoted without approval, evidence or verification is an exception regardless of whether the value is now correct.
testing.done: every sampled change shows pre-dated approvals, matching test evidence and a post-implementation export.

testing.step: Test access restriction on the configuration objects
actions: Extract current membership of the DORA configuration role and compare it to the latest attestation approved by the CISO.
Confirm no leaver retains membership and that every joiner has a dated approval.
Attempt a threshold edit with a general administrator account in the cloned instance and confirm it is denied.
Read the SOC alert history for role-membership changes and direct table edits in the period.
testing.done: role membership matches the attestation, general administrators are denied, and SOC alerting is evidenced.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the configuration object, the expected and found values, and the period the wrong value was live.
Assess and record whether any incident in that period was classified or timed under the wrong value, and notify the Incident Response Lead where it was.
Assign a root cause — stale standard after an ESA change, out-of-change edit, missing approval, untested scenario — and an owner with a remediation date.
Carry every open issue into the next quarterly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, an incident-impact assessment, a root cause, an owner and a remediation date.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the drift rate against the standard and the change-compliance rate against the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the production export, the timer re-performance and the boundary tests.
Have the independent reviewer, who holds no write access to the configuration and approved none of the sampled changes, sign the workpaper.
Report to the ICT Risk Committee and file under DORA / Configuration with the raw exports attached.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with drift rate, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

checklist.step: Segment the audience from the worker record, not from a memory of the org chart
actions: Extract all active workers of the EU legal entities at the cycle cut-off: employees, fixed-term staff, and contractors flagged as holding system access.
Tag each worker into an audience: all-staff baseline, ICT and incident-response, client-facing and complaint-handling, ICT third-party managers, senior management, management body member.
Join the IAM platform entitlement feed so anyone with production ICT access is captured even where their job title does not suggest it.
Send the audience counts to the Head of Compliance and record the extract date and row count as the population of record.
checklist.done: every active EU worker carries exactly one primary audience tag, reconciled to the IAM access feed.

checklist.step: Set the learning outcomes from the DORA articles
actions: Read Art. 13(6) and Art. 5(4) on EUR-Lex and write the outcome list each audience must demonstrate.
For all staff: recognise a potential ICT-related incident, know the reporting route and the awareness timestamp's importance, and know not to discuss an incident externally.
For ICT and incident-response staff: apply the Art. 18 classification criteria, start the 4h/24h clocks correctly, and know the 72-hour and one-month report obligations.
For client-facing staff: know when a client must be told under Art. 19(3) and the approved holding script; for third-party managers: know the Art. 28-30 contractual and register obligations.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm each outcome traces to an article before content is written.
checklist.done: each audience has counsel-confirmed learning outcomes, each traced to a named DORA article.

checklist.step: Build the modules against the outcomes with real incident material
actions: Build one module per audience in the LMS authoring tool, mapping every screen to an outcome id.
Use two anonymised real incidents from the firm's own post-incident reviews as worked scenarios, including one where classification was late.
Add a decision exercise for ICT staff that requires entering criterion values and reaching a major/not-major call against the thresholds.
Include the escalation contacts and the Art. 14(2) designated public contact by role name so learners know exactly who to call.
Publish content in every official language required by the entities' staff base.
checklist.done: each module maps screen by screen to outcomes, uses two real anonymised incidents, and exists in every required language.

checklist.step: Write the knowledge assessment with a defensible pass mark
actions: Write at least three questions per learning outcome, including scenario questions rather than definition recall.
Set the pass mark at 80% with a maximum of three attempts and randomised question order from a bank.
Configure the LMS to record score, attempt count and completion timestamp per learner.
Pilot the assessment with 15 staff across audiences and revise any question with a pass rate over 95% or under 40%.
checklist.done: the assessment covers every outcome, is piloted and revised, and records score, attempts and timestamp.

checklist.step: Get the curriculum approved before assignment
actions: Review the outcome-to-article mapping, the module content and the assessment blueprint.
Obtain the Chief Info Security Officer's approval of the technical accuracy and the Chief HR Officer's approval of the assignment and consequence model.
Record all three approvals with names and dates on the GRC control record by 31 January.
Version the curriculum and freeze it for the cycle; mid-cycle content changes require a new version and a re-approval.
checklist.done: the curriculum version carries dated Compliance, CISO and CHRO approvals recorded by 31 January.

checklist.step: Assign the modules and set the deadlines
actions: Load the audience-tagged population and assign each worker their audience module with a 30 June due date.
Configure the dynamic assignment rule so a worker moving into an ICT or client-facing role is auto-assigned the additional module within 24 hours of the HRIS change.
Set the new-joiner rule to assign the baseline module on day one with a 30-day deadline.
Confirm the assignment count equals the HRIS population count and investigate any difference before the campaign opens.
checklist.done: assignment count reconciles to the HRIS population, with dynamic and new-joiner rules live.

checklist.step: Deliver the Art. 5(4) session to the management body
actions: Schedule the dedicated ICT risk session for the management body ahead of the annual Art. 6(5) framework review.
Have the Chief Info Security Officer present the firm's ICT risk profile, the year's major incidents, the third-party concentration position and the resilience testing results.
Record attendance by name in the minutes, including apologies, and arrange a catch-up session for absentees within 30 days.
Post the deck and the minutes to the board portal and log the session against each member's LMS record.
checklist.done: the session is minuted with named attendance, absentees have a dated catch-up, and each member's LMS record shows it.

checklist.step: Run the completion campaign and escalate on the reminder ladder
actions: Publish a weekly completion dashboard by entity, audience and line manager from the LMS reporting module.
Fire reminders at 30, 14 and 3 days before 30 June, and escalate outstanding learners to their line manager on the deadline.
Escalate to the entity executive at deadline plus 14 days with the named list, not a percentage.
Ask the Access Management Analyst to prepare the access-restriction list for anyone outstanding at deadline plus 30 days.
checklist.done: reminders and escalations fired on schedule and the outstanding list is named down to the individual.

checklist.step: Give incident responders a live exercise rather than only a module
actions: Run a tabletop for the incident response and notification cell using an injected client-impacting outage scenario.
Require participants to complete the classification form, start the clocks, draft the client notice and dry-run the authority submission against the 4-hour window.
Record participation by name and the elapsed times achieved, and debrief every point where the team hesitated on a rule.
Feed the hesitation points back to the Instructional Designer as required content changes for the next version.
checklist.done: a named-attendance tabletop record exists with measured elapsed times and content-change feedback raised.

checklist.step: Train the ICT third-party managers on the register and contract obligations
actions: Deliver a workshop covering the Art. 28(3) register of information fields, the Art. 30 mandatory contractual provisions and the notification of planned arrangements supporting critical or important functions.
Walk the attendees through completing a real register row end to end, including the function-criticality assessment and the provider identifiers.
Set an exercise requiring each attendee to correct a deliberately defective register row and mark the results.
Record attendance and exercise scores against the LMS module so the evidence sits in one place.
checklist.done: third-party managers have a scored, attendance-recorded workshop covering register fields and Art. 30 clauses.

checklist.step: Close out non-completion with a documented consequence
actions: Take the named outstanding list at deadline plus 30 days and confirm each person's status — active, on leave, left, or genuinely non-compliant.
For active non-completers apply the agreed consequence: line manager meeting recorded on the worker record and, for ICT-access holders, suspension of privileged access until completion.
Record long-term absence and parental leave as deferrals with a return-to-work assignment date rather than as completions.
Obtain the Chief HR Officer's sign-off on the final disposition of the whole outstanding population.
checklist.done: every outstanding worker has a recorded disposition — completed, deferred with a date, or consequence applied — signed off by the CHRO.

checklist.step: Analyse assessment results for real knowledge gaps
actions: Build a report of pass rate, mean score and attempt count by question, audience and entity.
Identify questions failed by more than 30% of an audience and name the underlying outcome as a gap.
Cross-check the gaps against the year's incident post-mortems — where a gap matches a real failure, raise it as a priority content change.
Publish the analysis to the Head of Compliance and the CISO with the proposed content changes.
checklist.done: a gap analysis by outcome exists, cross-checked against real incidents, with proposed content changes.

checklist.step: Feed the training result into the Art. 6(5) framework review
actions: Prepare the training section of the annual framework review: completion by audience and entity, assessment gap analysis, tabletop performance and management body session evidence.
State plainly where the obligation was not met and what is being done, rather than presenting a rounded percentage.
Submit the section to the Corporate Secretary for inclusion in the management body's review pack.
Record the management body's comments as inputs to the next cycle's curriculum.
checklist.done: the framework review pack carries a training section with completion, gaps and named shortfalls, and board comments are captured.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum for the next cycle
actions: Take the gap analysis, tabletop feedback, board comments and any ESA guidance published in the year as the change list.
Rewrite the affected modules and refresh the incident scenarios with the current year's anonymised cases.
Retire the previous version in the LMS with a retirement date so nobody can be assigned stale content.
Submit the new version for approval by 31 January of the next cycle.
checklist.done: a new curriculum version exists driven by the gap list, with the prior version retired and dated.

checklist.step: File the training evidence pack
actions: Move the HRIS population extract, curriculum version with approvals, assignment and completion registers, assessment score export, tabletop and workshop records and the management body minutes into DORA / Training / <cycle year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-cycle-end retention label.
Confirm the pack is searchable by entity, audience and worker id.
Confirm the completion register is stored as an immutable export so later LMS changes cannot rewrite it.
checklist.done: the pack is filed immutably with a 10-year label and is searchable by entity, audience and worker id.

testing.step: Build the population of workers who owed the training
actions: Extract independently from the HRIS all active workers of the EU entities at the cycle cut-off, including contractors with system access and management body members.
Add anyone holding production ICT entitlements from the IAM platform feed who is absent from the HRIS extract.
Reconcile your population to the LMS assignment count and investigate every difference before sampling — an unassigned worker is the failure mode this test exists to find.
testing.done: an independently built population reconciles to LMS assignments with every difference explained.

testing.step: Re-perform the audience segmentation on a sample of roles
actions: Take 30 workers spanning job families and re-derive their audience tag from job title, entitlements and team.
Compare to the assigned tag and flag every ICT-access holder or client-facing worker who received only the baseline module.
Confirm every management body member is tagged for the Art. 5(4) session and not merely the all-staff module.
Record the re-derivation logic so the test is repeatable.
testing.done: sampled audience tags are independently re-derived and every under-assignment is raised.

testing.step: Draw and document the completion-record sample
actions: Take 100% of management body members, incident-response staff and ICT third-party managers.
Take 40 baseline-audience workers at random using a recorded seed, stratified by entity and language.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all critical audiences in full and is stratified by entity.

testing.step: Trace each sampled worker to a completion record with score and timestamp
actions: Open each sampled worker's LMS transcript and read the module version, completion timestamp, score and attempt count.
Confirm the completion timestamp is on or before 30 June, or within 30 days of start date for new joiners.
Confirm the module version completed is the approved current version, not a retired one.
Capture the transcript screen into the workpaper and flag any completion recorded by administrative override.
testing.done: each sampled worker shows a dated, in-window completion of the current module version at or above the pass mark.

testing.step: Verify the management body session against the minutes
actions: Open the minutes of the Art. 5(4) session on the board portal and read the named attendance and apologies.
Confirm the session pre-dates the annual Art. 6(5) framework review approval.
Confirm every absentee has a dated catch-up session recorded within 30 days.
Read the agenda and confirm it covered ICT risk profile, major incidents, third-party concentration and resilience testing — a generic governance update is a fail.
testing.done: the session is evidenced by minutes with named attendance, in-scope agenda, and catch-ups for every absentee.

testing.step: Re-perform the outcome-to-article mapping on the curriculum
actions: Read Art. 13(6) and Art. 5(4) and independently list what the training must cover for staff and for the management body.
Open the current module content and check each required topic is actually taught, not merely listed on a contents slide.
Confirm the ICT audience module teaches the Art. 18 classification criteria and the 4h/24h/72h/one-month windows explicitly.
Raise any missing topic as a content exception with the article reference.
testing.done: the curriculum is checked topic by topic against the independently derived article requirements.

testing.step: Recompute the completion rates against the thresholds
actions: Recompute completion by audience and entity from the raw LMS export joined to the HRIS population, without using the published dashboard.
Compare your rates to the reported figures and explain any difference above 0.5 percentage points.
Confirm deferrals for leave are excluded from the numerator and are not counted as completions.
Test the rates against the ≥98% baseline and 100% critical-audience thresholds and state pass or fail per audience.
testing.done: rates are independently recomputed from raw data, reconcile to the report, and are graded against each threshold.

testing.step: Test the non-completion consequences actually landed
actions: Take the named outstanding list at deadline plus 30 days and check each recorded disposition against the worker record.
For ICT-access holders who did not complete, confirm privileged access was actually suspended by reading the IAM entitlement history, not the intention on a spreadsheet.
Confirm the CHRO sign-off exists and post-dates the final disposition list.
Any non-completer who retained privileged access without a documented CISO exception is a fail.
testing.done: every consequence is evidenced in the IAM history or by a documented exception, with CHRO sign-off in place.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the worker population or the curriculum topic, the shortfall and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause — population feed gap, wrong audience tag, retired module assigned, escalation not fired, consequence not applied — and an owner.
Set remediation dates inside 60 days and require re-completion evidence rather than a management assertion.
Carry every open issue into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a re-completion evidence requirement.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the completion rate by audience, the assessment pass rate and the management body position against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the reconciliation, the transcripts and the minutes.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Compliance and L&D and delivered none of the sampled modules, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit Committee and the management body and file under DORA / Art. 13(6) training.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with rates by audience, a stated conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
