Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 19(3) (client impact and notification), Art. 13(1)-(2) (post-incident review and learning) and Art. 11(10) (client redress feeding aggregated costs and losses), read alongside the entity's national complaint-handling rules and EIOPA's complaints-handling guidelines

In-scope processes.value: Continuous complaint intake across contact centre, portal, broker and ombudsman channels → DORA cause tagging → linkage to the incident record → root-cause analysis → redress and remediation → theme reporting to the ICT Risk Committee

In-scope systems.value: Complaint case records with the DORA cause taxonomy; contact-centre interactions from Genesys Cloud, incident linkage from ServiceNow ITSM, and redress payments from the Policy Administration Platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: DORA Complaint Handling and Root-Cause Standard — the ICT cause taxonomy, the mandatory incident-linkage rule, redress principles for outage-caused loss, the 15-business-day acknowledgement and 8-week final-response clocks, and the monthly theme review

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Operating Officer; re-approved annually and after any incident that produced more than 50 linked complaints

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Complaint acknowledged within 5 business days and finally responded within 8 weeks under the entity's national rules; DORA cause tagging applied within 2 business days of intake; monthly theme pack to the ICT Risk Committee by the 10th working day

Deadline reminders configured.value: CRM case SLAs at 5 days and 8 weeks with supervisor escalation at 75%; an automatic alert to the Market Conduct manager when DORA-tagged complaint volume for a single incident passes 25 in a rolling 7 days

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Complaint case file, correspondence, incident linkage, root-cause record, redress calculation and payment evidence, retained 10 years from case closure alongside the incident record

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: An ICT-caused complaint with no incident link, a missed final-response deadline, and a recurring root cause with no owned remediation are each logged as exceptions with owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off closure of every root-cause remediation and every redress methodology applied to a complaint cohort

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All complaints closed in the period for the EU entities, including untagged ones, plus all complaints linked to a major ICT-related incident and all ombudsman referrals citing service unavailability

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on ICT-caused complaints left untagged or unlinked to an incident; ≥98% final responses inside 8 weeks; any recurring root cause appearing in three consecutive months without a remediation owner is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous; testing runs monthly on the closed-case population with a quarterly deep dive on incident-linked cohorts and root-cause recurrence

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside the complaints-handling line and must not have handled or approved any sampled case

Evidence location for test results.value: Monthly complaint-conformance workpaper (case population, tagging re-performance, linkage test, redress recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under DORA / Complaints

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Complaint log export with DORA cause tags, linked incident references, response timings, redress paid and root-cause themes, presentable to the national competent authority or the ombudsman within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Market Conduct owns ombudsman and conduct-supervisor correspondence; the Head of Compliance owns anything that touches the DORA incident record and Regulatory Counsel clears admissions of ICT-caused client detriment

checklist.step: Capture the complaint with enough detail to identify an ICT cause
actions: Open a complaint case in the CRM and record channel, entity, product, client identifier and the client's own words describing what failed.
Capture the date, time and channel of the failed interaction — portal login, quote, claim submission, premium payment, benefit payment — because that is what links to an outage window.
Ask the client what financial detriment they suffered: late claim payment, missed renewal, duplicate charge, lapsed cover, and record amounts and dates.
Acknowledge in writing within 5 business days with the case reference and the named handler.
checklist.done: the case records the failed interaction's timestamp and channel, the claimed detriment, and a dated written acknowledgement.

checklist.step: Apply the DORA cause taxonomy within two business days
actions: Set the cause tag from the controlled list: service unavailability, transaction failure, data corruption or loss, delayed incident notification, third-party provider outage, or not ICT-related.
Where the description is ambiguous, ask the Contact Center Supervisor to pull the Genesys interaction recording and the portal session log before tagging.
Record the reason for the tag in a mandatory free-text field — the tag alone is not evidence.
Re-tag rather than close where later investigation changes the cause, keeping the tag history.
checklist.done: every case carries a taxonomy tag applied within 2 business days with a written reason and a preserved tag history.

checklist.step: Link each ICT-tagged complaint to the incident record that explains it
actions: Search ServiceNow for incidents whose affected services and outage window cover the client's failed interaction timestamp.
Write the incident number onto the complaint case and the complaint reference onto the incident's linked-complaints list so the relationship exists in both directions.
Where no incident covers the timestamp, raise a new incident with the client evidence attached — a complaint may be the first detection of an outage.
Flag to the Incident Response Lead any cluster of unlinked complaints sharing a service and window.
checklist.done: every ICT-tagged complaint carries a bidirectional incident link, or has triggered a new incident record.

checklist.step: Check whether the client should already have received an Art. 19(3) notice
actions: Open the notice log row for the linked incident and search the notified client population for the complainant's client id.
Where the incident was classified major and the client is absent from the population, raise a notification-completeness breach the same day.
Where the client is present but the complaint says no notice arrived, pull the dispatch record and bounce history and treat an undelivered notice as a delivery failure to remediate.
Record the finding on both the complaint case and the incident record.
checklist.done: each incident-linked complaint states whether the client was in the notified population and whether delivery succeeded.

checklist.step: Investigate and evidence the client's actual detriment
actions: Pull the transaction history for the client covering the outage window: premium collections, benefit and claim payments, policy status changes and portal transactions.
Compare what should have happened to what did, and quantify the delay in days and the amount involved.
Check for consequential effects — lapse for non-payment, late-payment interest, a claim decision delayed past its service standard — and quantify each.
Attach the transaction evidence to the case so the redress calculation is reproducible.
checklist.done: the case holds a quantified, evidenced detriment with the transaction history attached.

checklist.step: Calculate and pay redress on a consistent methodology
actions: Apply the published redress methodology: reverse incorrect charges, restore the policy position as if the outage had not occurred, pay interest on delayed payments at the standard rate, and add a distress-and-inconvenience amount from the published band.
Where a cohort shares one incident, apply the same methodology to every member and document the cohort definition rather than settling case by case.
Raise the payment in the policy administration system with the complaint reference in the payment narrative.
Record the redress amount against the linked incident so it flows into the Art. 11(10) aggregated cost-and-loss figure.
checklist.done: redress is calculated on the published methodology, paid with a traceable narrative, and posted to the incident's cost record.

checklist.step: Issue the final response inside the statutory window
actions: Draft the final response stating the finding, the cause in plain language, the redress and how it was calculated, and the client's onward rights including the ombudsman route and time limit.
Have the Complaints Manager review any response that denies an ICT cause where the case carries an incident link.
Send within 8 weeks of receipt and record the send timestamp and channel on the case.
Where 8 weeks cannot be met, send the holding letter the national rules require and record the reason for delay.
checklist.done: a final response with cause, redress basis and onward rights is sent inside 8 weeks with the timestamp recorded.

checklist.step: Aggregate the complaints per incident into a cohort view
actions: Build a per-incident cohort report: complaint count, channels, detriment types, total redress, response timings and open cases.
Compare the cohort size to the notified client population — a cohort much larger than expected suggests the population query missed clients.
Publish the cohort view on the incident record so the post-incident review sees the client impact in numbers.
Alert the Market Conduct manager where a cohort exceeds 25 complaints in a rolling 7 days.
checklist.done: each incident carries a cohort view with counts, redress totals and a comparison to the notified population.

checklist.step: Run root-cause analysis on the recurring themes, not on single cases
actions: Group the month's DORA-tagged complaints by affected service, cause tag and third-party provider.
For each group above the review threshold, run a five-whys with the service owner and the responsible ICT team and write the root cause in system terms.
Separate ICT root causes from process root causes — an outage the client was never told about is a notification-process failure, not an infrastructure failure.
Record each root cause with an owner and a target date in the Art. 13 learning-and-evolving register.
checklist.done: each recurring theme has a written root cause, separated into ICT and process causes, with an owner and target date.

checklist.step: Convert root causes into owned remediation actions
actions: Raise a remediation action per root cause with a named owner, a delivery date and the measure that will prove it worked.
Link the action to the control it strengthens — resilience testing scope, third-party contract terms, notification population query, or monitoring coverage.
Reject actions written as awareness or reminder activity where the cause is structural.
Report open actions past their date to the ICT Risk Committee by name and owner.
checklist.done: every root cause has a linked, measurable remediation action with an owner and a date.

checklist.step: Feed third-party-caused complaints into the provider governance cycle
actions: Extract complaints tagged third-party provider outage and group them by provider and contract.
Put the volume, detriment and redress cost on the agenda of the provider's next service review and minute the provider's response.
Check the contract's service levels and remedies against the actual outage and raise a service credit or breach notice where the terms allow.
Where the provider supports a critical or important function, feed the pattern into the concentration and exit-strategy assessment.
checklist.done: each affected provider has a minuted service review covering complaint volume, redress cost and contractual remedies.

checklist.step: Report the monthly DORA complaint pack
actions: Publish by the 10th working day: volumes by cause tag and entity, incident-linked cohorts, response timeliness, redress paid, open root causes and overdue remediation actions.
Show the trend against the prior six months so a deteriorating theme is visible rather than a single month's number.
Send to the ICT Risk Committee, the Head of Compliance and the CISO, and table it at the committee.
Record the committee's decisions and any new actions back onto the root-cause register.
checklist.done: the pack is issued by the 10th working day, tabled at the committee, and its decisions are recorded on the register.

checklist.step: Handle ombudsman and supervisor referrals as a distinct workstream
actions: Flag every case referred to the national ombudsman or raised by the conduct supervisor and assign it to a senior handler.
Assemble the referral pack: case file, incident record, notice log evidence, redress calculation and the final response.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the submission where it concedes ICT-caused detriment.
Record the outcome and, where the firm's position was overturned, raise a root cause on the decision logic that produced it.
checklist.done: each referral has a counsel-cleared pack, a recorded outcome, and a root cause raised on every overturn.

checklist.step: Re-test that closed remediations actually removed the cause
actions: Three months after each remediation closes, re-measure the complaint volume for that cause tag and service.
Compare against the pre-remediation baseline recorded when the action was raised.
Re-open the root cause where volume has not fallen, and record the re-open reason rather than raising a fresh action.
Report re-opened causes separately to the ICT Risk Committee.
checklist.done: every closed remediation has a three-month re-measurement against its baseline, with non-improvers re-opened.

checklist.step: File the complaint and root-cause evidence
actions: Move the monthly pack, cohort reports, root-cause records, remediation evidence and ombudsman outcomes into DORA / Complaints / <entity> / <year-month>.
Apply the 10-years-from-case-closure retention label and keep the link to the incident evidence pack intact.
Confirm the pack is searchable by incident reference, cause tag and client id.
Confirm redress payment evidence is retained with the case, not only in the ledger.
checklist.done: the pack is filed with a 10-year label, linked to the incident pack, and searchable by incident, cause tag and client.

testing.step: Build the population of complaints closed in the period
actions: Extract every complaint case closed in the period for the EU entities with channel, cause tag, receipt and final-response timestamps, linked incident and redress amount.
Add untagged and not-ICT-tagged cases — the population must include the cases the tagging may have wrongly excluded.
Reconcile the extract to the contact-centre complaint counts in Genesys and the ombudsman referral register, and resolve differences before sampling.
testing.done: the population reconciles across the CRM, the contact centre and the ombudsman register and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Re-perform the cause tagging on cases tagged not-ICT
actions: Take 40 cases tagged not-ICT-related whose narrative mentions outage, error message, failed payment, portal or system.
Read the narrative and the failed-interaction timestamp and independently decide the cause tag.
Cross-check each timestamp against the ServiceNow incident register for a covering outage window.
Any case that should have been ICT-tagged is a fail — this is the population the control most easily loses.
testing.done: not-ICT tags are independently re-derived on a targeted sample with every mis-tag raised as a fail.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of ICT-tagged cases
actions: Take 100% of cases linked to a major ICT-related incident and 100% of ombudsman referrals citing service unavailability.
Take 30 further ICT-tagged cases at random using a recorded seed, stratified by entity and cause tag.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all major-incident and ombudsman cases, and is stratified by entity and tag.

testing.step: Test the incident linkage in both directions
actions: For each sampled case, confirm the incident number on the case exists and that the case reference appears on the incident's linked-complaints list.
Confirm the client's failed-interaction timestamp falls inside the incident's recorded outage window for an affected service.
Take the reverse direction: for each major incident, check whether ICT-tagged complaints in its window went unlinked.
Any complaint whose timestamp matches an outage window but carries no link is an exception.
testing.done: linkage is proven in both directions with timestamps inside the recorded outage windows.

testing.step: Test notification completeness using the complaint cohort
actions: For each major incident, take the complainant client ids and check each against the notified client population on the notice log.
Count complainants absent from the notified population — each is evidence the Art. 19(3) population query under-selected.
Where the client was in the population, read the dispatch record and confirm delivery, treating an unresolved bounce as a failure.
Report the absent-complainant count per incident as a completeness metric in the workpaper.
testing.done: every complainant is checked against the notified population and absences are quantified per incident.

testing.step: Recompute redress on a sample and test cohort consistency
actions: Take 15 redressed cases and recompute the amount from the attached transaction history using the published methodology, including interest days and the distress band.
Compare to the amount paid and investigate any difference over 5% or EUR 50.
Take one incident cohort and confirm every member received the same methodology, not case-by-case negotiation.
Confirm the redress totals posted to the incident record match the payments made in the administration system.
testing.done: redress is recomputed within tolerance, applied consistently across the cohort, and reconciles to the incident cost record.

testing.step: Recompute the response-timeliness clocks
actions: Recompute acknowledgement elapsed days against 5 business days and final-response elapsed time against 8 weeks from the raw receipt timestamps.
Compare to the reported timeliness figures and explain any difference above 0.5 percentage points.
Confirm holding letters exist for every case exceeding 8 weeks and that the delay reason is recorded.
Check for cases re-opened and re-closed in a way that resets the clock and treat any found as an exception.
testing.done: timeliness is recomputed from raw timestamps, reconciles to the report, and clock-reset behaviour is tested.

testing.step: Test root-cause recurrence and remediation effectiveness
actions: List cause-tag and service combinations appearing in three or more consecutive months in the period.
For each, confirm a root cause is recorded with an owner and a remediation action, and read whether the action addresses the cause structurally.
For remediations closed more than three months ago, compare current volume to the recorded baseline and flag those with no reduction.
Any recurring theme with no owned action is a fail against the stated threshold.
testing.done: every recurring theme is checked for an owned structural action and closed remediations are re-measured against baseline.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the case or cohort, the failure and the client-detriment consequence.
Assign a root cause — tagging judgement, missing incident link, under-selected notification population, redress inconsistency, clock reset — and an owner.
Where clients were left unnotified or under-redressed, require a remediation sweep of the whole cohort rather than fixing only the sampled cases.
Carry every open issue into the next monthly test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner and, where clients were affected, a cohort-wide remediation sweep.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the mis-tagging rate, the unlinked-complaint rate, the timeliness rate and the absent-complainant counts against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the tagging re-performance, the linkage test and the redress recomputation.
Have the independent reviewer, who handled no sampled case, sign the workpaper.
Report to the ICT Risk Committee and the conduct governance forum and file under DORA / Complaints.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with the stated rates, a conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.

In-scope systems.value: Engagement planning, workpapers, findings and follow-up; evidence pulled from ServiceNow ITSM, the Policy Administration Platform correspondence history and the GRC notice log

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Audit Executive and tabled with the audit committee as part of the annual audit plan; the programme is refreshed whenever an ESA template or delegated act changes the criteria

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Engagement in the approved annual plan; fieldwork complete 8 weeks before the audit committee meeting that precedes the Art. 6(5) framework review; draft report to management within 10 business days of fieldwork close and final report within 30

Deadline reminders configured.value: AuditBoard milestone alerts at planning, fieldwork close, draft issue and final issue; automatic overdue alerts on management actions at due date and at due date plus 30 days to the Chief Audit Executive

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Engagement file — programme, population extracts with reconciliations, sample selection record, re-performance workpapers, screenshots, findings and management responses — retained 10 years from report issue

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Audit findings are raised with a rating, a management response, an accountable owner and a due date; overdue actions escalate to the audit committee rather than being re-dated by management

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CAE signs the closure of every finding only on re-tested evidence, and reports any action closed without evidence to the audit committee

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every major-incident notification set issued in the year — client notices, broker and counterparty variants, and the initial, intermediate and final authority reports — across all EU entities, plus the prior-year finding register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a missing mandatory content element, a missed statutory window, and an affected client left unnotified; an engagement is not reportable as complete if population reconciliation leaves any unexplained difference

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Engagement quality review by the CAE or a designated senior auditor who performed none of the fieldwork; the audited teams review for factual accuracy only

Evidence location for test results.value: AuditBoard engagement file with the signed report, cross-referenced to the compliance evidence repository under DORA / Internal Audit / <year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed audit report with scope, criteria, population, sample, findings, ratings and management actions, releasable to the national competent authority on request as Art. 6(6) evidence within 5 business days
