checklist.step: Scope the engagement and confirm auditor competence
actions: Open the annual plan entry and set the scope: EU entities, notice types, and the period from 1 January to 31 December.
Staff the engagement with auditors who hold demonstrable ICT and incident-management knowledge as Art. 6(6) requires, and record their qualifications in the engagement file.
Declare and resolve independence conflicts — no auditor may test a process they advised on in the year.
Issue the engagement notification to the CISO, the Head of Compliance and the Policy Admin Ops Lead with the evidence request list attached.
checklist.done: the engagement is scoped, staffed with evidenced ICT competence, independence-cleared and formally notified.

checklist.step: Fix the audit criteria from the primary sources before looking at any notice
actions: Read Art. 19(1),(3) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 on EUR-Lex and write the criteria grid: mandatory content elements per notice type and the four statutory windows.
Add the firm's own tighter internal standards separately so a breach of internal policy is not reported as a regulatory breach.
Have Regulatory Counsel confirm the criteria grid is complete and current before fieldwork opens.
Version and freeze the grid in the engagement file with the source consolidation dates.
checklist.done: a counsel-confirmed, version-frozen criteria grid exists with regulatory and internal standards separated.

checklist.step: Build the notification population from three independent sources
actions: Extract all incidents classified major in the year with their awareness and classification timestamps.
Extract the GRC notice log rows and the Internal Regulatory System submission receipts for the same period.
Extract the correspondence dispatch history for DORA template ids from the Policy Administration Platform.
Reconcile the three extracts row by row and document every difference and its explanation before sampling.
checklist.done: the population is built from three independent sources and reconciled with every difference explained in writing.

checklist.step: Test the completeness of the major-incident population itself
actions: Pull the year's availability breaches and security events from the SIEM and the service-monitoring feed.
Identify events with client-facing impact that never received a DORA classification form, and list them as candidate unreported incidents.
Re-apply the Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772 criteria to each candidate using the measured impact data.
Escalate immediately, without waiting for the report, any candidate that meets the major thresholds.
checklist.done: candidate unreported incidents are identified from monitoring data and re-classified, with immediate escalation of any major.

checklist.step: Select and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of major incidents and 100% of authority submissions — the population is small and each carries a statutory window.
Draw 40 client notices at random with a recorded seed, stratified by entity, channel and language, with a minimum of 5 per entity.
Record the seed, population sizes, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn.
Note explicitly which sub-populations were not sampled and why.
checklist.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all incidents and submissions, and its exclusions are stated.

checklist.step: Grade each sampled notice against the content criteria grid
actions: Open the rendered notice as the client received it, not the template, and mark each criterion present, partial or absent with the quoted sentence.
Confirm the notice states the impact on the client's financial interests and the mitigation measures taken, in language a policyholder can act on.
Confirm the template version used was the approved version on the dispatch date.
Check one non-English rendering per entity against the certified translation.
checklist.done: every sampled notice has a criterion-by-criterion grade with quoted sentences and a version check.

checklist.step: Recompute every statutory window from source timestamps
actions: Read awareness and classification timestamps from the incident audit history and normalise to UTC.
Recompute classification-to-initial against 4 hours, awareness-to-initial against 24 hours, initial-to-intermediate against 72 hours and intermediate-to-final against one month.
Recompute classification-to-first-client-dispatch and assess it against the without-undue-delay standard, stating the threshold used.
Compare every recomputed figure to the notice log and treat differences as findings in their own right.
checklist.done: all five elapsed times are recomputed from audit-history timestamps and reconciled to the notice log.

checklist.step: Re-derive the affected-client population independently
actions: Rebuild the affected-client list for two incidents from the affected services and outage window, writing your own query rather than re-running theirs.
Compare your list to the notified population and investigate every client present in yours and absent from theirs.
Corroborate with the linked complaint cohort and the failed-payment records for the window.
Quantify the under-notification as a client count and a percentage of your derived population.
checklist.done: an independently derived population exists for two incidents with under-notification quantified.

checklist.step: Verify the authority submissions against their receipts and field content
actions: Open each submission and read the authority reference number, submission timestamp and the entity identifiers including LEI.
Check every mandatory field of the Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 template is populated and internally consistent across the initial, intermediate and final reports.
Compare the final report's cost and loss figures to the ledger-based figures and query any unexplained movement.
Treat a missing receipt as a non-submission until the authority reference is produced.
checklist.done: each submission is evidenced by a receipt with complete, internally consistent mandatory fields.

checklist.step: Walk the notification process end to end with the operators
actions: Sit with the incident response and correspondence teams and walk one real incident from detection to final report, asking them to show each system action.
Note every point where the runbook and the actual practice diverge and record who decided the divergence.
Test the fallback paths by asking what happens when the authority channel is down and requiring them to show the documented alternative.
Record the walkthrough with names, dates and screenshots in the engagement file.
checklist.done: a dated walkthrough record exists naming every divergence between runbook and practice.

checklist.step: Follow up the prior-year findings before writing new ones
actions: Pull the prior-year DORA findings and their management actions with due dates and closure evidence.
Re-test each closed action against its original finding rather than accepting the closure memo.
Re-open any action whose evidence does not demonstrate the cause was removed, and record the re-open reason.
Report actions overdue by more than 90 days to the audit committee by owner name.
checklist.done: every prior-year action is re-tested on evidence, with unsupported closures re-opened and overdue actions named.

checklist.step: Rate the findings and agree management actions
actions: Rate each finding on the standard scale, treating a missed statutory window or an unnotified client as high or critical by definition.
Issue the draft to the CISO, the Head of Compliance and the Policy Admin Ops Lead for factual accuracy only, on a 10-business-day clock.
Require each action to name a single accountable owner, a delivery date and the evidence that will prove closure — reject actions written as reviews.
Record management disagreement verbatim rather than negotiating the finding away.
checklist.done: every finding is rated with a single-owner action, a date, a closure-evidence definition, and disagreements recorded verbatim.

checklist.step: Issue the report to the audit committee and the management body
actions: Issue the final report within 30 business days of fieldwork close with scope, criteria, population, sample, findings, ratings and actions.
State an overall opinion on the DORA notification process and say explicitly whether any client went unnotified or any window was missed.
Table the report at the audit committee ahead of the Art. 6(5) framework review and minute the committee's direction.
Publish the report to the board portal for the management body's review pack.
checklist.done: a final report with an overall opinion is tabled at the audit committee and published to the board portal.

checklist.step: Run the Art. 6(7) formal follow-up on open actions
actions: Track every open action monthly with owner, due date and evidence status.
Escalate at due date to the owner's executive and at due date plus 30 days to the audit committee chair.
Refuse a date extension unless the owner supplies a revised plan approved by the accountable executive, and record every extension.
Close only on re-tested evidence signed by the auditor who performed the re-test.
checklist.done: open actions are tracked monthly, escalated on schedule, and closed only on signed re-test evidence.

checklist.step: File the engagement evidence
actions: Cross-file the AuditBoard engagement export — programme, criteria grid, population reconciliations, sample record, workpapers, report and management responses — under DORA / Internal Audit / <year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-report-issue retention label.
Confirm the pack is searchable by incident reference, entity and finding id.
Confirm the workpapers are locked after issue so post-issue edits are impossible.
checklist.done: the engagement file is cross-filed, locked, retention-labelled and searchable by incident, entity and finding id.

testing.step: Build the population of engagements and findings claimed for the year
actions: Extract the approved annual audit plan entries covering DORA and the engagements actually delivered, with planned and actual dates.
Extract all findings raised, their ratings, owners, due dates and closure status.
Reconcile delivered engagements to the plan and list any planned DORA coverage that was deferred or dropped, with the approval that permitted it.
testing.done: delivered coverage reconciles to the approved plan with every deferral evidenced by an approval.

testing.step: Verify auditor competence and independence as Art. 6(6) requires
actions: Read the engagement staffing record and the recorded ICT qualifications and experience of each auditor.
Confirm no auditor tested a process they designed, advised on or operated during the period, by checking the independence declarations against their prior-year assignments.
Confirm the engagement quality reviewer performed none of the fieldwork.
A generic assertion of competence without named qualifications is a fail.
testing.done: auditor ICT competence and independence are evidenced by name, with the quality reviewer confirmed segregated.

testing.step: Draw and document the workpaper sample
actions: Take 100% of high and critical findings and 100% of workpapers covering authority submissions.
Take 12 further workpapers at random using a recorded seed across content grading, timing recomputation and population re-derivation.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers all high-rated findings and all submission workpapers.

testing.step: Re-perform the criteria grid from the legal text
actions: Independently derive the mandatory content elements and the four windows from Art. 19 and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/302 without reading the audit's grid.
Compare to the frozen criteria grid and raise any missing element or stale window as an audit-scope exception.
Confirm regulatory criteria and internal standards are kept separate so findings are correctly characterised.
Capture the source texts and consolidation dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: the audit's criteria grid is independently re-derived from primary sources with any gap raised.

testing.step: Re-perform the population reconciliation the audit relied on
actions: Re-extract major incidents, notice log rows and submission receipts for the period and reconcile them independently.
Compare your reconciliation to the audit's and investigate any row the audit explained away.
Confirm the audit's SIEM-based completeness test genuinely covered client-facing availability breaches, not only security events.
Any population difference the audit did not surface is an exception against the engagement.
testing.done: the population reconciliation is independently reproduced with every audit explanation tested.

testing.step: Re-perform the timing recomputation on sampled incidents
actions: Take five sampled incidents and recompute the four statutory windows plus classification-to-first-dispatch from the audit-history timestamps.
Compare to the audit's recorded figures and to the notice log, and investigate any difference greater than 15 minutes.
Confirm the audit used the classification timestamp for the 4-hour clock and the awareness timestamp for the 24-hour clock, not the same field for both.
Capture the timestamp evidence into the workpaper.
testing.done: the audit's timing figures are independently reproduced within 15 minutes on every re-tested incident.

testing.step: Re-grade sampled notices against the criteria
actions: Take 10 notices the audit graded compliant and grade them independently against the re-derived criteria.
Fail any notice lacking the financial-interest impact statement or the mitigation measures, even where the audit passed it.
Check the audit graded the rendered notice rather than the template, by comparing the artefact referenced in the workpaper.
Raise every grading difference as an engagement quality exception.
testing.done: re-graded notices either confirm the audit's conclusion or produce a documented grading difference.

testing.step: Test the follow-up discipline on closed findings
actions: Take 10 findings closed in the period and read the closure evidence against the original finding wording.
Confirm closure was signed by an auditor who re-tested, not by the action owner asserting completion.
List every action whose due date was extended and confirm each extension has an executive-approved revised plan.
Any closure without re-test evidence is a fail on the Art. 6(7) follow-up process.
testing.done: sampled closures are supported by signed re-test evidence and every extension carries an approved revised plan.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the engagement, the workpaper or finding, and the consequence for reliance on the audit.
Assign a root cause — stale criteria grid, incomplete population, template graded instead of render, closure without re-test, competence not evidenced — and an owner.
Where the audit missed a regulatory breach, escalate that breach directly to the Head of Compliance the same day, separately from the quality issue.
Carry every open issue into the next engagement's planning as a mandatory scope item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner and, where a breach was missed, a same-day escalation.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State the re-performance agreement rate, the criteria-completeness result and the follow-up closure quality against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion on whether the Art. 6(6) audit can be relied on as evidence of the framework's audit coverage.
Have the quality reviewer, who performed none of the fieldwork, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and file under DORA / Internal Audit with the engagement export attached.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with agreement rates, a reliance conclusion and an audit committee reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the charters, agendas, reservations of authority and minutes that evidence management body accountability for the ICT risk framework in each EU insurance and reinsurance entity

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 5 (management body ultimate responsibility, defined duties, ICT budget, ICT third-party arrangements, training) and Art. 6(1),(5) (documented framework reviewed at least once a year and after major incidents, supervisory instructions or resilience testing conclusions), applicable from 17 January 2025

In-scope processes.value: Governance operating cycle for each EU entity: charter maintenance → annual agenda plan → ICT risk reporting into the management body and its risk/audit committees → framework approval and review → decision and minute capture → delegation and reservation register upkeep

In-scope systems.value: Charters, agendas, papers, minutes, attendance and resolutions for the management body and the risk, audit and ICT risk committees; the underlying ICT risk reporting comes from the GRC platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: DORA Governance Standard — committee architecture per entity, the Art. 5(2) duties mapped to a named body, the annual agenda calendar, the minimum content of the ICT risk report, the framework approval resolution wording, and the trigger list forcing an off-cycle review

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the management body of each EU entity on the General Counsel's recommendation; reviewed annually and whenever the entity structure, committee composition or supervisory expectations change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Framework review and approval at least once a year and additionally on each major ICT-related incident, each supervisory instruction and each conclusion from resilience testing or audit; ICT risk report to the risk committee each quarter; ICT budget approved in the annual budget cycle

Deadline reminders configured.value: Board portal calendar tasks for each agenda item with papers due 7 calendar days before the meeting; an automatic off-cycle review task raised from the GRC platform whenever an incident is classified major or a supervisory instruction is logged

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Charters with version history, agendas, papers, minutes, attendance registers, resolutions and the delegation register, retained 10 years from the end of the financial year per the corporate records standard

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed annual review, an Art. 5(2) duty with no named accountable body, a major incident with no off-cycle review, and an inquorate approval are each logged as governance exceptions with owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: General Counsel signs off every charter amendment and every remediation of a defective or missing management body approval

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All management body, risk committee and audit committee meetings of the EU entities in the year, with their agendas, papers, attendance and minutes, plus the charter set, the delegation register and the trigger log of major incidents and supervisory instructions

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — an Art. 5(2) duty unassigned, a year without a documented framework review and approval, a major incident with no off-cycle review, or an approval taken without quorum is a fail; papers issued late in more than 10% of meetings is a fail on process

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is continuous with an annual review point; testing runs semi-annually over the meeting population and immediately after any major incident to confirm the off-cycle review happened

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not be the minute-taker or paper author for any sampled meeting

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual governance-conformance workpaper (meeting population, agenda coverage matrix, minute re-performance, trigger reconciliation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under DORA / Governance

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Charter set, Art. 5(2) duty-to-body map, annual agenda calendar with coverage evidence, framework approval resolutions and the ICT risk reports, producible for the national competent authority within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Corporate Secretary supplies governance records to the supervisor through the Head of Compliance; the management body chair responds on questions of board effectiveness with General Counsel present

checklist.step: Map every Art. 5(2) duty to a named body and a named individual
actions: Read Art. 5(2) on EUR-Lex and list each duty: approve and oversee the ICT strategy and framework, set roles and responsibilities for ICT functions, approve the digital operational resilience strategy, approve and review the ICT third-party service arrangements policy, set the ICT budget including awareness and resilience training, and set incident reporting arrangements.
Assign each duty to a specific body — management body, risk committee, audit committee — and to a named executive who prepares it.
Record any duty currently unassigned as a gap and raise it to the General Counsel the same week.
Publish the duty-to-body map as a controlled document referenced from each charter.
checklist.done: every Art. 5(2) duty has a named body, a named executive preparer and no gaps outstanding.

checklist.step: Update the charters so the DORA duties are actually written into terms of reference
actions: Open each entity's management body and committee charters on the board portal and insert the assigned duties verbatim from the duty-to-body map.
State the reporting lines: who reports ICT risk to the committee, how often, and what the report must contain as a minimum.
Add the quorum, conflict and written-resolution rules that will govern the framework approval so an approval cannot be taken inquorate.
Route the amended charters to the General Counsel for legal review and then to the body itself for adoption by resolution.
checklist.done: each charter carries the assigned duties verbatim, the reporting minimums and quorum rules, adopted by resolution.

checklist.step: Confirm the committee composition carries the required ICT knowledge
actions: Build a skills matrix for the management body and the risk committee showing ICT, cyber and operational resilience experience per member.
Identify where the body relies on a single member for ICT knowledge and record it as a key-person risk.
Where the matrix shows a gap, propose an appointment, an advisory attendee or a targeted training plan under Art. 5(4).
Refresh the matrix on every appointment and resignation and table it annually.
checklist.done: a current skills matrix exists per body with gaps named and a proposed remedy for each.

checklist.step: Set the annual agenda calendar so every duty lands in a meeting
actions: Build the calendar mapping each Art. 5(2) duty and the Art. 6(5) framework review to a specific meeting date in the year.
Place the framework review before the financial year end and after the annual resilience testing results are available.
Place the ICT risk report on every quarterly risk committee agenda and the Art. 5(4) session before the framework review.
Circulate the calendar to the CISO, the Chief Risk Officer and the Head of Compliance so paper owners know their dates.
checklist.done: every duty and the framework review are calendared to a named meeting date with paper owners informed.

checklist.step: Specify the minimum content of the ICT risk report
actions: Define the standing report sections: ICT risk profile against appetite, major incidents with client impact and notification timeliness, resilience testing results including TLPT status, ICT third-party concentration and register position, audit findings and overdue actions, and the ICT budget position.
Require quantified data — incident counts, clients affected, redress paid, window breaches — rather than narrative assurance.
Agree the data sources so the report reconciles to the notice log, the register of information and the audit finding register.
Have the management body approve the report specification so a thin paper can be rejected on a defined basis.
checklist.done: an approved report specification exists naming every section, its quantified metrics and its reconciling data source.

checklist.step: Produce and issue the papers with time to read them
actions: Collect papers from the named owners against the report specification and reject any paper missing a required section.
Upload to the board portal at least 7 calendar days before the meeting and record the issue timestamp.
Flag late papers to the chair before the meeting so the chair can decide whether the item can be taken at all.
Restrict paper access to members and named attendees and log every access.
checklist.done: papers are complete against the specification, issued 7 days ahead with a recorded timestamp, and access-logged.

checklist.step: Run the annual Art. 6(5) framework review and take the approval resolution
actions: Table the ICT risk management framework document with the year's changes marked, the resilience testing conclusions and the internal audit opinion.
Confirm quorum before the vote and record it in the minute.
Take a resolution in explicit terms — that the management body approves the ICT risk management framework version <n> and has reviewed it under Art. 6(5) — rather than noting the paper.
Record the version number approved and attach the approved document to the minute.
checklist.done: a quorate resolution approving a named framework version under Art. 6(5) is minuted with the document attached.

checklist.step: Trigger an off-cycle review when the regulation demands it
actions: Maintain a trigger log capturing every major ICT-related incident, every supervisory instruction or finding, and every conclusion from resilience testing or audit.
Raise an off-cycle framework review task to the Corporate Secretary within 5 business days of each trigger.
Prepare the review paper stating what the trigger revealed and which framework sections need to change.
Track each trigger to a minuted board or committee consideration and close it only on that reference.
checklist.done: every trigger has a raised review task and closes only against a minuted board or committee consideration.

checklist.step: Approve the ICT budget as an explicit board decision
actions: Present the ICT and resilience budget as a distinct line in the annual budget paper, separating awareness training, resilience testing, incident response capability and third-party risk management.
Show the prior-year spend against approval and explain material underspend on resilience activity.
Have the management body approve the budget by resolution referencing Art. 5(2) so the approval is identifiable.
Report in-year reallocations away from resilience lines back to the risk committee.
checklist.done: the ICT and resilience budget is approved by an identifiable resolution with prior-year spend explained.

checklist.step: Approve the ICT third-party policy and see the register position
actions: Table the ICT third-party service arrangements policy for approval and review, with the changes since last approval marked.
Present the register of information position: arrangements supporting critical or important functions, concentration by provider and by ICT service type, and the exit strategies in place.
Flag planned arrangements supporting critical or important functions so the body sees them before they are contracted.
Minute the body's decisions on any concentration the policy would not permit.
checklist.done: the policy is approved by resolution and the register and concentration position are minuted with decisions recorded.

checklist.step: Write minutes that evidence challenge, not just attendance
actions: Record attendance by name including apologies, the quorum, and any conflict declared and how it was handled.
Minute the questions members asked on ICT risk and the answers given, so the record shows challenge rather than receipt.
Record each decision as a resolution with its wording, the vote, and any dissent.
Draft within 10 business days, circulate for comment, and have the chair approve at the following meeting.
checklist.done: minutes show named attendance, quorum, recorded challenge, resolution wording and chair approval at the next meeting.

checklist.step: Track board actions to closure
actions: Maintain an action register with owner, due date, the minute reference that created it and the evidence required to close it.
Report the register at every meeting showing overdue items by owner name.
Escalate any ICT risk action overdue by more than one meeting cycle to the chair in advance of the meeting.
Close actions only against the evidence named when the action was raised.
checklist.done: the action register ties every item to a minute reference and closes only on the named evidence.

checklist.step: Keep the delegation and reservation register aligned to the charters
actions: Maintain the register of matters reserved to the management body and those delegated, with the delegate named and the limit stated.
Confirm the DORA duties that Art. 5 places on the management body are shown as reserved and not delegated to management.
Re-approve the register annually and after any committee restructure, recording the approving resolution.
Test one delegated decision a quarter against the register to confirm the delegate acted within the stated limit.
checklist.done: the register is current, shows the Art. 5 duties as reserved, and is re-approved by resolution annually.

checklist.step: Assess board effectiveness on ICT risk oversight
actions: Run an annual questionnaire asking members whether ICT risk information was timely, quantified and sufficient to challenge.
Interview the CISO and Chief Risk Officer on whether the body's challenge changed any decision in the year.
Write the findings with specific improvement actions — earlier papers, deeper metrics, more frequent deep dives — with owners and dates.
Table the assessment at the management body and minute its response.
checklist.done: an annual effectiveness assessment on ICT oversight exists with owned actions and a minuted board response.

checklist.step: File the governance evidence pack
actions: Cross-file charters with version history, the duty-to-body map, agenda calendar, papers, minutes, attendance registers, resolutions and the delegation register under DORA / Governance / <entity> / <year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-financial-year-end retention label.
Confirm the pack is searchable by entity, meeting date and resolution reference.
Confirm approved minutes are locked so post-approval edits are impossible.
checklist.done: the pack is filed, locked, retention-labelled and searchable by entity, meeting date and resolution reference.

testing.step: Build the population of meetings, papers and resolutions
actions: Extract every management body, risk committee and audit committee meeting of the EU entities in the period with date, agenda, papers, attendance and minutes status.
Extract the resolution register and the action register for the same period.
Reconcile the meeting count to the scheduled calendar and list every cancelled or postponed meeting with the reason and what happened to its agenda items.
testing.done: the meeting population reconciles to the calendar with every cancellation and its agenda consequence explained.

testing.step: Test the Art. 5(2) duty-to-body map for completeness
actions: Independently list the Art. 5(2) duties from EUR-Lex without reading the firm's map.
Compare to the duty-to-body map and to the charters themselves — a duty in the map but absent from the charter is still unassigned.
Confirm the charters place these duties on the management body and not on management, and check the delegation register agrees.
Raise any unassigned or wrongly delegated duty as a fail.
testing.done: every Art. 5(2) duty is independently traced into a charter with the delegation register agreeing.

testing.step: Draw and document the meeting sample
actions: Take 100% of meetings at which the framework was approved or reviewed, the ICT third-party policy was approved, or the ICT budget was set.
Take 8 further meetings at random using a recorded seed, spread across entities and committees.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every framework, third-party policy and budget decision meeting.

testing.step: Re-perform the agenda coverage matrix against the calendar
actions: Build your own matrix of duty against meeting date from the actual agendas and minutes, not from the planned calendar.
Confirm the Art. 6(5) framework review occurred at least once in the year and that the quarterly ICT risk report was tabled in each quarter.
Identify any duty that was calendared but deferred without being re-scheduled and landed.
A duty calendared and never taken is a fail regardless of the plan's existence.
testing.done: an independently built coverage matrix proves each duty was actually taken, with deferrals traced to a later meeting.

testing.step: Verify the framework approval resolution and its quorum
actions: Open the minute of the framework approval and read the resolution wording, the version number approved and the vote.
Count attendees against the charter quorum and confirm the minute records quorum as met before the vote.
Confirm the approved framework version attached to the minute matches the version held as current in the GRC platform.
A minute that notes the paper without resolving to approve is a fail against Art. 6(5).
testing.done: the approval is evidenced by an explicit, quorate resolution naming the framework version held as current.

testing.step: Reconcile the trigger log to off-cycle reviews
actions: Extract every major ICT-related incident, supervisory instruction and resilience testing or audit conclusion in the period, independently of the trigger log.
Match each to a minuted board or committee consideration and read whether the framework implications were actually discussed.
Measure the elapsed days from trigger to consideration and flag anything beyond one meeting cycle.
Any trigger with no minuted consideration is a fail against Art. 6(5).
testing.done: every independently identified trigger traces to a minuted consideration with the elapsed time measured.

testing.step: Test paper timeliness and content sufficiency
actions: For each sampled meeting, read the paper upload timestamps and compute days before the meeting against the 7-day standard.
Grade the ICT risk report against the approved report specification section by section and mark missing or unquantified sections.
Reconcile the report's incident counts and notification timeliness figures to the notice log and its register figures to the register of information.
Raise both late issue and specification shortfalls as exceptions.
testing.done: paper timeliness is computed per meeting and the ICT risk report is graded and reconciled to source systems.

testing.step: Test minute quality for evidence of challenge and decision
actions: Read the sampled minutes for named attendance, quorum, declared conflicts, recorded questions and answers, and resolution wording with the vote.
Compare the minute to the paper — where the paper raised a risk the minute does not address, record it as a challenge gap.
Confirm the chair approved the minute at the following meeting and that the approved version is locked.
Trace three actions from the minute to the action register and to their closure evidence.
testing.done: sampled minutes evidence quorum, challenge and resolution wording, with actions traced to closure evidence.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, the body, the meeting date and the duty or approval affected.
Assign a root cause — duty never mapped, charter not updated, calendar item deferred, paper late, minute silent on the decision, trigger not escalated — and an owner.
Where an approval is missing or inquorate, require the body to re-take the decision at its next meeting rather than back-fixing the minute.
Carry every open issue into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner and, for defective approvals, a re-take at the next meeting.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State duty coverage, framework review completion, trigger response rate and paper timeliness against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the coverage matrix, the resolution evidence and the trigger reconciliation.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no sampled paper and took no sampled minute, sign the workpaper.
Report to the audit committee and the management body and file under DORA / Governance.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with coverage rates, a stated conclusion and a board reporting date exists in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the DORA governance filings made by each EU entity — the annual register of information, notifications of planned critical arrangements, the Art. 11(10) cost-and-loss estimate and the framework review attestation — with the Regulatory Reporting Manager executing the submissions

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 Art. 28(3) (register of information reported at least yearly and timely notification of planned arrangements on critical or important functions), Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956 (register templates), Art. 11(10) (aggregated annual costs and losses on request) and Art. 6(5), together with the national competent authority's submission instructions

In-scope processes.value: Annual and event-driven filing cycle per EU entity: register of information assembly from contracts and the CMDB → validation against the ESA templates → competent authority submission at the reference date → event-driven notifications of planned critical arrangements → on-request Art. 11(10) statement → filing register closure

In-scope systems.value: Submission packaging, validation and receipts to the national competent authority; source data from Icertis CLM for contracts, the CMDB for ICT services and the GRC platform for function criticality

Compliance procedure documented.value: DORA Regulatory Filing Procedure — filing calendar per entity, the register data-owner map by template, the validation rule set, the LEI and provider-identifier standard, the four-eyes review, the submission route and fallback, and the receipt filing rule

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Corporate Secretary countersigning the governance content; re-approved whenever the ESAs revise the templates or the national competent authority changes its submission instructions

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Register of information submitted at least yearly at the reference date and by the deadline the national competent authority publishes for the annual ESA collection; planned arrangements supporting critical or important functions notified in a timely manner before contracting; Art. 11(10) estimate delivered by the date stated in the authority's request; framework review evidence available at the annual review

Deadline reminders configured.value: Filing calendar tasks at T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-7 days to each submission deadline, with escalation to the Head of Compliance at T-14 if validation has not passed; an automatic task on any new contract flagged as supporting a critical or important function

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submitted register files, validation reports, four-eyes review records, authority receipts, notification letters and the Art. 11(10) statement with its ledger reconciliation, retained 10 years from submission

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A late or rejected submission, a critical arrangement contracted without prior notification, and any register row failing validation at the reference date are logged as filing exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every re-submission and every notification made late, and approves the explanation given to the competent authority

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All DORA filings due in the period per entity — annual register submissions, notifications of planned critical arrangements, Art. 11(10) responses — plus every ICT third-party contract signed or amended in the period as the completeness source for the register

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — a missed or late submission, a critical arrangement contracted without prior notification, or a register row omitted where a contract exists is a fail; register validation must pass with zero blocking errors before submission

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with event-driven notifications; testing runs once after each annual submission and quarterly on the event-driven notification population

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have assembled or submitted the filing under test; where the manager submitted, the review passes to the Head of Compliance

Evidence location for test results.value: Filing-conformance workpaper (contract population, register reconciliation, validation output, submission receipts, notification timing analysis, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under DORA / Filings / <entity> / <year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Submitted register files with their authority receipts, the notification correspondence, the Art. 11(10) statement with its ledger tie-out and the approval trail, producible for the national competent authority or EIOPA within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager handles submission queries and resubmission requests; the Head of Compliance owns any explanation of a late or defective filing and Regulatory Counsel clears it before it is sent

checklist.step: Build the filing calendar per EU entity from the authority's instructions
actions: Read the national competent authority's current DORA reporting instructions and the ESA annual collection notice, and record the reference date, the submission deadline and the accepted file format.
Create one calendar row per entity per filing: annual register of information, event-driven notifications, and any on-request obligation open at the time.
Record the submission channel and the technical validation rules the authority applies, including file naming and encoding.
Set T-90/T-60/T-30/T-7 reminders and name the preparer and the reviewer on every row.
checklist.done: every entity has calendar rows with reference date, deadline, channel, format, preparer and reviewer named.

checklist.step: Assemble the contract population that the register must describe
actions: Extract from Icertis every contractual arrangement for the use of ICT services in force at the reference date, including intra-group arrangements and subcontracted chains.
Cross-check against accounts-payable spend on ICT vendors in the ERP to find arrangements never entered into the CLM.
Cross-check against the CMDB for applications and hosting whose provider is external, to find shadow arrangements.
Reconcile the three sources and record every difference with its resolution before any template is populated.
checklist.done: the contract population is reconciled across the CLM, ICT spend and the CMDB with all differences resolved.

checklist.step: Assess and record which functions are critical or important
actions: Take the business function inventory and apply the criticality criteria — impact on the entity's ability to meet obligations to policyholders, financial soundness, and continuity of insurance and reinsurance activities.
Map each ICT service in the contract population to the functions it supports and inherit the criticality.
Have the function owner and the Chief Risk Officer confirm each critical or important designation in writing.
Record the assessment date and rationale on each row — the designation drives both the register content and the notification duty.
checklist.done: every ICT service carries a confirmed criticality designation with a dated rationale and a named confirming owner.

checklist.step: Populate the register templates field by field
actions: Open the current Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956 template set and populate each template in turn: entity information, contractual arrangements, ICT third-party service providers, ICT services, functions supported, subcontracting chains and assessments.

Enter the LEI for the reporting entity and for each provider where one exists, and the EUID or the specified alternative identifier where it does not — an identifier field left blank fails validation.
Enter annual expense or estimated cost per arrangement, the start and end dates, the governing law and the countries where data is stored and processed.
Populate the linkage keys consistently so arrangements, providers, services and functions join across templates without orphans.
checklist.done: every template is populated with valid identifiers and consistent linkage keys, with no orphan rows across templates.

checklist.step: Run the validation rules before anyone sees the file
actions: Run the authority's technical validation and the internal rule set: mandatory fields, code-list conformity, identifier format, date logic, and cross-template referential integrity.
Fix at source — correct the contract record in Icertis or the criticality in the GRC platform — rather than editing the extract, so the next cycle inherits the correction.
Re-run until zero blocking errors remain and record every warning with a written rationale for accepting it.
Attach the final validation report to the filing calendar row.
checklist.done: validation passes with zero blocking errors, every warning is rationalised, and fixes were made at source.

checklist.step: Reconcile the register to the prior submission and explain the movement
actions: Compare row counts and key fields against the prior year's submitted register by arrangement identifier.
Produce a movement schedule: new arrangements, terminated arrangements, criticality reclassifications and provider changes, each with a reason.
Investigate any arrangement that disappeared without a termination and any provider whose identifier changed without a corporate event.
Attach the movement schedule to the submission pack so the authority's questions can be answered from the file.
checklist.done: a movement schedule explains every difference from the prior submission with no unexplained disappearances.

checklist.step: Run four-eyes review before submission
actions: Review the populated templates against the source contracts for a sample of at least 20 arrangements including every critical or important one.
Check the criticality designations against the confirmations from the function owners and the Chief Risk Officer.
Confirm the entity identifiers, the reference date and the reporting entity scope are correct for the submitting entity.
Sign the review record; the preparer may not also be the reviewer.
checklist.done: a signed four-eyes review covers the critical arrangements and confirms entity scope and reference date.

checklist.step: Obtain the internal approval that authorises the filing
actions: Present the register summary and the movement schedule to the risk committee or the delegated approver named in the filing procedure.
Record the approval with name, role and date, and note any condition attached to it.
Where the register reveals a concentration outside appetite, ensure that is minuted as a decision rather than buried in the filing.
Release the file for submission only once the approval is recorded.
checklist.done: a named, dated approval exists on the record before the file is released for submission.

checklist.step: Submit to the national competent authority and capture the receipt
actions: Package the file to the authority's naming and format specification and submit through the designated channel before the published deadline.
Capture the submission timestamp and the authority's acknowledgement or reference number.
Where the authority returns technical errors, correct and resubmit inside the deadline and record both attempts.
Use the documented fallback route and record the attempt times if the channel is unavailable — never let the deadline pass silently.
checklist.done: the file is submitted before the deadline with an authority acknowledgement reference recorded.

checklist.step: Notify planned arrangements on critical or important functions before contracting
actions: Configure the Icertis workflow so any draft contract flagged as supporting a critical or important function raises a notification task before signature approval.
Prepare the notification to the competent authority describing the provider, the ICT services, the functions supported and the planned start date.
Send in time for the authority to consider it before the arrangement is entered into, and record the sent date and any authority response.
Block contract execution in the workflow until the notification is recorded as sent.
checklist.done: no critical or important arrangement can be executed without a recorded, pre-signature notification.

checklist.step: Prepare the Art. 11(10) aggregated cost-and-loss statement on request
actions: On receipt of the authority's request, log it on the filing calendar with the stated response date and the exact scope asked for.
Extract the named ledger accounts and cost centres for the financial year and total gross costs and losses by major incident reference, showing recoveries separately.
Tie the total to the final incident reports already submitted so the authority sees consistent figures, and explain any difference in a note.
Have the Controller confirm the ledger tie-out in writing before the statement is released.
checklist.done: the statement ties to the ledger and to the submitted final reports, with a written Controller confirmation.

checklist.step: Answer authority follow-up questions from the filed pack
actions: Log every supervisory query against the filing with the date received and the response deadline.
Draft the response from the submitted pack and the movement schedule, never from a fresh extract that would produce different numbers.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any response that concedes an error or omission in a submitted register.
File the query, the response and any resubmission together with the original submission.
checklist.done: every query has a logged response drawn from the filed pack, counsel-cleared where it concedes an error.

checklist.step: Correct and resubmit when an error is found after filing
actions: Assess the materiality of the error — omitted arrangement, wrong criticality, wrong identifier — and record the assessment.
Correct at source, re-run validation and resubmit under the authority's resubmission procedure, referencing the original submission.
Notify the competent authority of the correction with a short explanation cleared by Regulatory Counsel.
Raise a GRC exception with root cause so the same error cannot repeat next cycle.
checklist.done: the correction is resubmitted with an authority reference, a cleared explanation and a root-caused GRC exception.

checklist.step: Report the filing position to the management body
actions: Table a filing status paper at the risk committee: filings due, filings made, deadlines met, resubmissions, open queries and any notification made late.
Show the register's concentration picture so the body sees what its own filing tells the supervisor.
Minute the body's decisions on any concentration or dependency it will not accept.
Carry unresolved items to the next meeting rather than closing them on assurance.
checklist.done: a filing status paper is tabled and minuted, including late notifications and concentration decisions.

checklist.step: File the submission evidence pack
actions: Move the submitted files, validation reports, movement schedule, four-eyes review, approval record, authority receipts, notification correspondence and query responses into DORA / Filings / <entity> / <year>.
Apply the 10-years-from-submission retention label.
Confirm the pack is searchable by entity, filing type, reference date and authority reference number.
Confirm the submitted file is stored byte-identical to what was sent, not a later working copy.
checklist.done: the pack holds the byte-identical submitted file with receipts, retention-labelled and searchable by authority reference.

testing.step: Build the population of filings due and ICT contracts signed
actions: Extract the filing calendar rows for the period per entity and the submissions actually made with their timestamps and authority references.
Extract independently from Icertis every ICT contract signed, amended or terminated in the period, with its criticality flag.
Reconcile filings due to filings made and list every gap with its explanation before sampling.
testing.done: filings due reconcile to filings made and the contract population is independently extracted.

testing.step: Test register completeness against contracts and spend
actions: Take the ICT vendor spend for the year from the ledger and match each vendor to a register row for the submitting entity.
Investigate every vendor with ICT spend and no register row, and read the contract to decide whether an arrangement for the use of ICT services exists.
Cross-check the CMDB for externally hosted applications whose provider does not appear in the register.
Any arrangement in force at the reference date with no register row is a fail.
testing.done: register completeness is tested from ledger spend and the CMDB, with every unmatched provider investigated.

testing.step: Draw and document the register-row sample
actions: Take 100% of rows flagged as supporting a critical or important function and 100% of rows with subcontracting chains recorded.
Take 25 further rows at random using a recorded seed, stratified by entity and provider.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers every critical arrangement and every subcontracting chain.

testing.step: Trace sampled rows field by field to the contract
actions: Open the executed contract for each sampled row and compare the register values for provider identifier, ICT service type, start and end dates, governing law, data location and annual cost.
Confirm the LEI or specified alternative identifier is present and matches the legal entity that actually contracted.
Confirm subcontracting chains recorded in the register match the subcontractors the contract permits or discloses.
Capture the contract page evidencing each disputed field into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled row is traced field by field to the executed contract with evidence captured for disputed fields.

testing.step: Re-perform the criticality assessment independently
actions: Take 12 arrangements, including some designated non-critical, and re-apply the criticality criteria against the functions they support.
Compare to the recorded designation and treat an understated criticality as a fail — it removes both register detail and the notification duty.
Confirm the function owner and Chief Risk Officer confirmations exist in writing and pre-date the submission.
Record the criteria values you used so the judgement is reproducible.
testing.done: criticality is independently re-derived on a mixed sample with every understatement raised as a fail.

testing.step: Re-run validation on the submitted file
actions: Take the byte-identical submitted file from the evidence pack and re-run the authority's technical validation and the cross-template referential checks.
Confirm zero blocking errors and read every accepted warning against its recorded rationale.
Check for orphan rows — an arrangement with no provider, a service with no function — that referential validation would allow but that make the register unusable.
Any blocking error on the submitted file is a fail regardless of the receipt.
testing.done: the submitted file re-validates clean with warnings rationalised and no orphan rows.

testing.step: Verify submission timing and receipts against the deadlines
actions: Read the published deadline from the competent authority's instruction and compare it to the submission timestamp on the receipt.
Confirm the reference date on the file matches the reference date the authority specified.
For resubmissions, confirm the correction was made under the authority's resubmission procedure and referenced the original.
Treat a missing receipt as a non-submission until the authority reference is produced.
testing.done: every submission is evidenced by a receipt inside the published deadline with the correct reference date.

testing.step: Test the pre-contract notification of critical arrangements
actions: Take every contract signed in the period supporting a critical or important function and read its signature date.
Find the notification to the competent authority and compare the sent date to the signature date.
Any arrangement contracted before the notification was sent is a fail against Art. 28(3); measure the days by which it was late.
Test the Icertis workflow block by attempting to advance a flagged draft without a recorded notification.
testing.done: every critical arrangement shows a notification pre-dating signature and the workflow block is proven to work.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception naming the entity, the filing, the row or arrangement and the regulatory consequence.
Assign a root cause — contract never entered in the CLM, criticality understated, identifier missing, deadline missed, notification bypassed — and an owner.
For omitted arrangements or late notifications, require a resubmission or a notification with a counsel-cleared explanation to the authority.
Carry every open issue into the next filing cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner and, where the authority was misinformed, a cleared correction.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State register completeness, field accuracy, criticality agreement, on-time submission and notification timeliness against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the ledger-based completeness test, the contract tracing and the receipts.
Have the independent reviewer, who neither assembled nor submitted the filings under test, sign the workpaper.
Report to the risk committee and the management body and file under DORA / Filings with the submitted files attached.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with completeness and timeliness rates, a conclusion and a committee reporting date exists in the repository.
